docs.text: You do not have to describe anything: a normal controller already gets docs (see What Dox fills in for you). When you want better text, put annotations on the controller method. They are all in dox_core.

docs.title: Adding a summary and tags
docs.text:
@Summary is the short title, @Description is the longer text, and @Tags puts the route in a group:

class BlogController {
  @Summary('Get one blog')
  @Description('Deleted blogs are not found.')
  @Tags(<String>['Blogs'])
  Future<Blog?> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
    return Blog().find(id);
  }
}

@Tags also works on the class. Here is what you get for GET /blogs/{id} with AuthMiddleware on the route:

get:
  tags: [Blogs]
  summary: Get one blog
  description: Deleted blogs are not found.
  operationId: BlogController.show
  parameters:
    - {name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}
  responses:
    "200":
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Blog"}
    "401": {description: Not logged in}
    "404": {description: Not found}
    "500": {description: Server error}
  security:
    - bearerAuth: []

docs.title: Using doc comments
docs.text:
A /// comment on a method also sets the summary and the description. The first line is the summary, and the rest is the description:

/// Get one blog
///
/// Deleted blogs are not found.
Future<Blog?> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
  return Blog().find(id);
}

When a method has both, the annotation wins.

docs.title: Adding responses
docs.text:
Use @Response to describe an answer. Add more than one for more status codes:

@Summary('Log in')
@Request(LoginUser)
@Response(200, LoginResult)
@Response(401, null, description: 'Wrong email or password')
Future<dynamic> login(DoxRequest req) async { ... }

The type can be a model, List<User>, a @Dto, a Serializer or a basic type like String. When you add a 2xx response, the return type of the method is not used.

docs.title: Hiding a route
docs.text:
@ApiIgnore() leaves a method, or a whole class, out of the docs:

@ApiIgnore()
Future<void> internal(DoxRequest req) async { ... }

To leave out routes by path, use include and exclude in the config.

docs.title: Marking a route as deprecated
docs.text:
Use @ApiDeprecated(). The Dart @Deprecated annotation works too:

@ApiDeprecated()
Future<List<Blog>> oldIndex() async { ... }

docs.title: Describing the request
docs.text:
The builder finds the request class of a method in this order. The first one wins:

  1. @Body(T), @Query(T) or @Request(T) on the method.
  2. An argument whose type is a @Dto class, like store(CreateBlog body).
  3. A req.validate<T>() call in the method, where T is a @Dto class.

For POST, PUT and PATCH, the request is the JSON body. For other methods, each field is one query parameter. @Body and @Query pick the place by hand, and so does @Dto(source: Source.query).

@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 200)
  final String title;

  /// Text of the blog.
  final String? description;   // nullable: optional

  final int views;             // default: optional, `default: 0`

  final Status status;         // enum: only `draft` or `published`

  final List<Tag> tags;        // a list of another @Dto class

  const CreateBlog({required this.title, this.description, this.views = 0,
      required this.status, required this.tags});
}

The keys in the docs are the keys the DTO reads: snake_case by default, or @Name('key'). Each rule adds its JSON Schema keys, see the rules reference.

docs.title: Describing the response
docs.text:
The return type of the method gives the 200 answer. Future<T> counts as T.

Return type Schema a model (@DoxModel) $ref to the model. Keys in hidden are left out List<Model> an array of the model a @Dto class $ref to the class a Serializer<Model> the map that convert() returns, else the model Pagination total, per_page, last_page, current_page, data String, int, bool, Map, List the basic JSON type dynamic the types of the return values. A map literal gives its keys DoxResponse, void no schema

A model schema has the primary key, the @Column fields, created_at, updated_at, the relations (only when they are loaded) and the @Computed getters. It goes in components/schemas:

Blog:
  type: object
  properties:
    id: {type: integer}
    title: {type: [string, "null"]}
    user: {anyOf: [{$ref: "#/components/schemas/User"}, {type: "null"}]}
    created_at: {type: [string, "null"], format: date-time}

docs.title: Login schemes
docs.text:
The docs page needs to know how a route is protected, so "Try it" can send a token. Put @Security above a middleware class. Every route with this middleware then gets the scheme:

/// `Authorization: Bearer <api key>`. Not a JWT.
@Security.bearer(format: 'API key')
class ApiKeyAuthMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware { ... }

@Security.bearer() gives type: http, scheme: bearer. The format becomes bearerFormat, like bearerFormat: JWT for format: 'JWT'.

For a key in a header, use @Security.apiKey. The default header is X-API-Key:

@Security.apiKey(header: 'X-API-Key')
class HeaderKeyMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware { ... }

Run dart run build_runner build after you add it. The scheme name is the class name without Middleware, with a small first letter: ApiKeyAuthMiddleware gives apiKeyAuth. Use scheme: 'myName' to pick another name.

A middleware without @Security whose class name ends with AuthMiddleware gets bearerAuth: a bearer token with no format.

docs.title: Setting schemes in the config
docs.text:
For a key in the query or a cookie, set the scheme in the config. The config wins over @Security:

OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  securitySchemes: <String, SecurityScheme>{
    'apiKey': SecurityScheme.apiKey(name: 'X-API-Key'),
  },
  securityByMiddleware: <String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>>{
    'ApiKeyMiddleware': <Map<String, List<String>>>[
      <String, List<String>>{'apiKey': <String>[]},
    ],
  },
);

docs.title: What Dox fills in for you
docs.text:
A controller with no annotations already gets docs. Annotations only change the result.

Part of the docs Where it comes from path, method the route table path param types the controller arguments after the first one, in order. int id gives integer tags the class name without Controller (BlogController gives Blog) operationId Class.method, like BlogController.show summary, description the annotations, else the /// comment request see Describing the request 200 answer the return type, see Describing the response 401 and a login scheme see Login schemes 401 and 403 the Can middleware, or a req.authorize(...) call in the method 403 the GuestMiddleware or ValidateSignature middleware, or a Gate.authorize(...) call in the method 404 the path has a {param} 422 the route has a request class, or the method calls req.validate<T>() or req.validateSchema(...) 500 every route

A @Response with the same status wins over an automatic answer. Routes the builder does not know, like inline closures, still get a basic entry.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Option Default What it does enabled null true or false turns the docs on or off. null: on only when APP_ENV is development or local info Info(title: 'Dox API', version: '1.0.0') title and version of the API servers [] base URLs, like [Server('https://api.my.app')] registry empty openApiRegistry from lib/generated/openapi.g.dart securitySchemes, securityByMiddleware {} see Login schemes ui DocsUi.scalar the docs page: DocsUi.scalar or DocsUi.swagger scalar ScalarOptions() see Changing the docs page pageTitle info.title title of the /docs page include [] (all routes) only these paths go in the docs, like ['/api/*'] exclude [] these paths are left out, like ['/api/internal/*']

docs.title: Turn the docs on in production
docs.text:
By default the docs are off in production. If you have a public API and want the docs there too, set enabled: true:

lib/config/openapi.dart
OpenApiConfig openApi = OpenApiConfig(
  enabled: true,
  info: Info(title: 'Blog API', version: '1.0.0'),
  registry: openApiRegistry,
);

/docs has no login, so anyone can see every route of your API. Only do this for a public API. enabled: false turns the docs off everywhere.

docs.title: Changing the docs page
docs.text:
Change the look of the Scalar page with scalar::

OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  pageTitle: 'Blog API docs',
  scalar: ScalarOptions(theme: ScalarTheme.purple, darkMode: true),
);
Option Default What it does theme ScalarTheme.default_ color theme, like moon, purple, deepSpace, saturn, kepler or mars darkMode false start in dark mode. The user can still switch showDownloadButton true show the button that downloads the document proxyUrl null send "Try it" requests through this proxy. Without it, requests go from the browser straight to your API

To use Swagger UI instead, set ui::

OpenApiConfig(registry: openApiRegistry, ui: DocsUi.swagger);

docs.title: Write the files
docs.text:
Sometimes you want the document as files, for example to give it to a client generator. Use dox openapi:generate:

dox openapi:generate              # storage/openapi/openapi.json and openapi.yaml
dox openapi:generate docs/api     # another folder

It runs bin/openapi.dart of your app. A new app does not have this file, so make it:

bin/openapi.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  await Dox().writeOpenApi(args.isEmpty ? 'storage/openapi' : args.first);
  exit(0);
}

writeOpenApi runs your providers and registers the routes. It does not start the server.

docs.title: Production setup
docs.text:
enabled: true is the quick way to show the docs in production. The other way is to make the document at build time, put the files in the image, and serve the files. The URLs stay the same.

You need lib/config/openapi.dart (see Setup) and bin/openapi.dart (see Write the files).

  1. Make both files, if you do not have them yet.

  2. Add a controller that serves the files:

    lib/app/http/controllers/docs.controller.dart
    import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_openapi/dox_openapi.dart'
    show OpenApiConstants, OpenApiServer;
import 'package:my_app/config/openapi.dart';

@Inject()
class DocsController {
  /// The same Scalar page as the live docs. It loads `/openapi.json`.
  final String _page = OpenApiServer(
    OpenApi(info: openApi.info),
    pageTitle: openApi.pageTitle,
    ui: openApi.ui,
    scalar: openApi.scalar,
  ).docsPage().body;

  DoxResponse page() {
    return response(_page)
        .contentType(ContentType.parse(OpenApiConstants.htmlContentType));
  }

  DoxResponse json() {
    return _file('openapi.json', OpenApiConstants.jsonContentType);
  }

  DoxResponse yaml() {
    return _file('openapi.yaml', OpenApiConstants.yamlContentType);
  }

  DoxResponse _file(String name, String contentType) {
    File file = File('docs/openapi/$name');
    if (!file.existsSync()) throw NotFoundHttpException();
    return response(file.readAsStringSync())
        .contentType(ContentType.parse(contentType));
  }
}

    If your pubspec.yaml has no dox_openapi, run dart pub add dox_openapi. Run the builder again after you add the controller.

  3. Add the routes. Add them only when the live docs are off, so they do not clash in development:

    lib/routes/web.dart
    @override
void register() {
  if (!openApi.isEnabled) {
    Route.get('/docs', (DocsController c) => c.page);
    Route.get('/openapi.json', (DocsController c) => c.json);
    Route.get('/openapi.yaml', (DocsController c) => c.yaml);
  }
  // ...
}

    Import openApi from lib/config/openapi.dart, and the controller, in this file.

  4. Make the files in the Docker build and copy them into the image. In the build stage, right after RUN /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox build, add:

    Dockerfile
    RUN APP_KEY=only-for-the-build-not-a-key /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox openapi:generate docs/openapi

    Then, in the RUN step that lays out /out, add /out/app/docs to mkdir -p and copy the files after the cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/ line:

    Dockerfile
    RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/app/docs /out/tmp \
  && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
  && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/ \
  && cp -r docs/openapi /out/app/docs/openapi \
  # ... the lines that follow stay as they are

    bin/openapi.dart loads your app config, so it needs an APP_KEY. The dummy key is only for this step and is not in the image. If a provider connects to a database in setup(), that database must be reachable in the build step.

  5. Start the image with APP_ENV=production and open /docs.

These routes have no login, so anyone can see every route of your API. To protect them, put a middleware on the three routes.

To test it on your machine, run dox openapi:generate docs/openapi, then start the app with APP_ENV=production.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dox_openapi also works on its own. Describe each route by hand with ApiDoc:

import 'package:dox_openapi/dox_openapi.dart';

ApiDoc docs = ApiDoc();
Map<String, dynamic> user = docs.schema('User', userSchema); // returns a $ref

docs.route('GET', '/users/{id}',
    summary: 'Get one user',
    tags: <String>['users'],
    params: <String, Object>{'id': <String, dynamic>{'type': 'integer'}},
    responses: <int, ResponseDoc>{
      200: ResponseDoc(schema: user, description: 'The user'),
      404: const ResponseDoc(description: 'Not found'),
    });

OpenApi api = OpenApi(info: const Info(title: 'My API', version: '1.0.0'), docs: docs);

A schema can be a JSON Schema Map, a dox_validation schema, or any object with toJsonSchema(). Paths can use {id} or :id.

docs.title: Getting the document
docs.text:
api.toJson();                              // Map
api.toJsonString();                        // pretty JSON
api.toYaml();                              // YAML
await api.writeFiles('storage/openapi');   // openapi.json + openapi.yaml

docs.title: Serving the docs from your own server
docs.text:
OpenApiServer gives the page and the document for a path:

OpenApiServer server = OpenApiServer(api); // Swagger UI: OpenApiServer(api, ui: DocsUi.swagger)
OpenApiResponse? page = server.handle('/docs'); // also '/openapi.json' and '/openapi.yaml'
if (page != null) {
  // send page.body with the header Content-Type: page.contentType
}

docs.title: Text response keys
docs.text:
responses takes status codes as int keys. For a text key like default or 2XX, use namedResponses. It wins when the same key is in both:

docs.route('GET', '/users/{id}',
    responses: <int, ResponseDoc>{
      200: ResponseDoc(schema: user, description: 'The user'),
    },
    namedResponses: <String, ResponseDoc>{
      'default': const ResponseDoc(description: 'Any other error'),
    });

DoxRouteAdapter().addTo(docs, routes) adds a basic entry for each route you did not describe.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
• Each annotation also has a lower case name, like @summary('Log in'). Only @Response has none, because response() is already a dox_core helper.
  • @DoxController(tag: 'Users') is for a class that the builder can not see in a Route.get(...) call.
  • The route body: option still works, and it wins over the request class.
  • @Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field) keeps the field names as keys.
  • The document is built on the first /docs request, then kept.
  • The page loads Scalar from the jsDelivr CDN at a fixed version. pageTitle and all options are escaped.
  • An optional param shows as two paths, because OpenAPI path params must be required. /blog/{id?} gives /blog/{id} and /blog. The short path gets no 404, and its own summary and operation id.
  • GuestMiddleware(redirectTo: ...) shows a 403, but the app sends a redirect. Add @Response(403, ...) to replace it.
  • Can, GuestMiddleware and ValidateSignature are found by class name. Gate.authorize(...) is found when Gate is the class of dox_auth.
  • At runtime, Dox matches each route to its docs by method name, HTTP method and the end of the path. Group prefixes do not matter. When two controllers have a method with the same name, name the class in the route, like (LinkController c) => c.index.

docs.title: PDF Library
docs.text:
Create, load and edit PDF files in Dart with dox_pdf_lib, and send them from a Dox controller.

dox_pdf_lib draws text, shapes, SVG paths, JPEG and PNG images. It also does forms, attachments, metadata, custom fonts, and PDF/A and PDF/X. It has the API of the pdf-lib JavaScript library.

The package is standalone. It does not need Dox, and Dox does not need it. To fill pdfme templates, see pdfme.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: dart pub add dox_pdf_lib

docs.title: Sending a PDF from a controller
docs.text:
A controller can return a DownloadableFile. Dox streams the bytes and sets Content-Type and Content-Disposition. The browser saves the file. See Response.

Use StreamFile instead to show the PDF in the browser tab.

lib/app/http/controllers/report.controller.dart
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_pdf_lib/dox_pdf_lib.dart';

@Inject()
class ReportController {
  Future<DownloadableFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
    PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.create();
    PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.helvetica);
    PDFPage page = doc.addPage(PageSizes.A4);
    page.drawText('Monthly report', x: 50, y: 750, font: font, size: 24);

    Uint8List bytes = await doc.save();
    return DownloadableFile(
      ContentType('application', 'pdf'),
      Stream<List<int>>.value(bytes),
      'report.pdf',
      length: bytes.length,
    );
  }
}
lib/routes/api.dart
Route.get('/report.pdf', (ReportController c) => c.show);

docs.title: Using other fonts
docs.text:
The 14 standard PDF fonts, like Helvetica, are built in. They only have Latin letters. For other languages, embed your own TrueType or OpenType font. Use subset: true to put only the letters you use into the file.

Uint8List bytes = File('NotoSansThai-Regular.ttf').readAsBytesSync();
PDFFont thai = await doc.embedFont(bytes, subset: true);
page.drawText('สวัสดีครับ', x: 50, y: 700, font: thai, size: 20);

Thai, Myanmar, Khmer, Lao, Arabic, Hebrew and Hindi text is laid out correctly. Line breaks in Myanmar, Thai, Khmer and Lao go between words.

docs.title: PDF/A and PDF/X
docs.text:
PDF/A is for long-term archives. PDF/X is for print. One call, setConformance, sets up a document for the standard you pick.

You bring the ICC profile. The package ships none.

Uint8List srgb = File('sRGB2014.icc').readAsBytesSync();

PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.create();
doc.setTitle('Annual report');
doc.setConformance(
  PDFStandard.pdfA2b,
  iccProfile: srgb,
  outputConditionIdentifier: 'sRGB IEC61966-2.1',
);

// PDF/A needs fonts from a font file. Standard fonts do not work.
PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(
  File('NotoSans-Regular.ttf').readAsBytesSync(),
  subset: true,
);
doc.addPage().drawText('Kept for a long time', x: 50, y: 750, font: font);

for (ConformanceIssue issue in doc.checkConformance(PDFStandard.pdfA2b)) {
  print(issue);
}

checkConformance lists what is still wrong. For PDF/X, use PDFStandard.pdfX1a, pdfX3 or pdfX4, and give each page a trim box. The dox_pdf_lib README has the full list of rules.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text:
dox_pdf_lib uses dart:ffi and a small native library. It runs in Dart programs on macOS, Linux and Windows.

It does not run on the web, iOS or Android.

A ready-built native library is downloaded for you, so you do not need Rust.

On Linux, the ready-built library needs glibc 2.35 or newer, for example Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12. On older Linux, or on Alpine, build the library yourself. The dox_pdf_lib README shows how.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
The same code works in any Dart program. Call PDFDocument.create(), then write the bytes to a file:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_pdf_lib/dox_pdf_lib.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  PDFDocument doc = await PDFDocument.create();
  PDFFont font = await doc.embedFont(StandardFonts.helvetica);
  PDFPage page = doc.addPage(PageSizes.A4);
  page.drawText('Hello, PDF!', x: 50, y: 750, font: font, size: 30);
  File('hello.pdf').writeAsBytesSync(await doc.save());
}

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• dox_pdf_lib on pub.dev: pages, forms, attachments, images, metadata and the full API.
  • Source on GitHub

docs.title: pdfme
docs.text:
Make PDF files from pdfme templates in Dart with dox_pdf_me, and send them from a Dox controller.

You design the template in the pdfme designer, then fill it with data on the server. dox_pdf_me reads the same template JSON as pdfme, and the PDF looks the same.

The package is standalone. It does not need Dox, and Dox does not need it. It is built on PDF Library.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: dart pub add dox_pdf_me

docs.title: Filling a template
docs.text:
Design the template in the pdfme designer and save its JSON. Read it with Template.fromJson. The inputs are one map of strings for each copy of the template.

A controller can return a DownloadableFile. Dox streams the bytes and sets Content-Type and Content-Disposition. The browser saves the file. See Response.

Use StreamFile instead to show the PDF in the browser tab.

lib/app/http/controllers/invoice.controller.dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_pdf_me/dox_pdf_me.dart';

@Inject()
class InvoiceController {
  Future<DownloadableFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
    Map<String, Object?> json =
        jsonDecode(File('storage/invoice.template.json').readAsStringSync())
            as Map<String, Object?>;

    Uint8List bytes = await generate(
      template: Template.fromJson(json),
      inputs: <Map<String, String>>[
        <String, String>{'customer': 'Jane Doe', 'total': '120.00'},
      ],
      plugins: builtInPlugins,
    );
    return DownloadableFile(
      ContentType('application', 'pdf'),
      Stream<List<int>>.value(bytes),
      'invoice.pdf',
      length: bytes.length,
    );
  }
}
lib/routes/api.dart
Route.get('/invoice.pdf', (InvoiceController c) => c.show);

dox_pdf_me supports text, image, svg, shapes, barcodes and QR codes, date and time, checkbox, radio group, select, table, multi variable text, signature and circle mark. Pass builtInPlugins to use all of them.

docs.title: Using other fonts
docs.text:
Text uses Roboto by default. For other languages, pass your fonts in GenerateOptions:

Uint8List noto = File('NotoSansJP-Regular.otf').readAsBytesSync();
Uint8List pdf = await generate(
  template: template,
  inputs: inputs,
  plugins: builtInPlugins,
  options: GenerateOptions(
    font: <String, FontSource>{
      'Roboto': FontStore.defaultFont,
      'NotoSansJP': FontSource(noto),
    },
  ),
);

Thai, Myanmar, Khmer, Lao, Arabic, Hebrew and Hindi text is laid out correctly. Line breaks in Myanmar, Thai, Khmer and Lao go between words.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text:
dox_pdf_me uses dox_pdf_lib, which has a small native library. It runs in Dart programs on macOS, Linux and Windows.

It does not run on the web, iOS or Android.

A ready-built native library is downloaded for you, so you do not need Rust.

On Linux, the ready-built library needs glibc 2.35 or newer, for example Ubuntu 22.04 or Debian 12. On older Linux, or on Alpine, build the library yourself. The dox_pdf_lib README shows how.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
The same code works in any Dart program. Call generate(...), then write the bytes to a file:

import 'dart:io';
import 'dart:typed_data';

import 'package:dox_pdf_me/dox_pdf_me.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  Uint8List pdf = await generate(
    template: Template(
      basePdf: const BlankPdf(),
      schemas: <List<Schema>>[
        <Schema>[
          const TextSchema(name: 'title', position: Position(20, 20), width: 170, height: 15),
          BarcodeSchema(name: 'link', barcodeType: BarcodeType.qrcode, position: const Position(20, 40)),
        ],
      ],
    ),
    inputs: <Map<String, String>>[
      <String, String>{'title': 'Hello, PDF!', 'link': 'https://dartondox.dev'},
    ],
    plugins: builtInPlugins,
  );
  File('hello.pdf').writeAsBytesSync(pdf);
}

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• dox_pdf_me on pub.dev: schema types, tables, plugins, fonts and options, and how to build a template in Dart.
  • Source on GitHub

docs.title: Socket.IO
docs.text:
dox_socketio is a Socket.IO v4 server for Dart, and it is the way to do realtime in Dox.

The official clients connect to it with no changes: socket.io-client (JavaScript v4) and the Dart socket_io_client package. It has acks, rooms, namespaces, binary data and long-polling.

In a Dox app, Socket.IO runs on the same port as your HTTP routes, at /socket.io/. It can also run on its own, see Without Dox.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The quick way is the CLI:

dox add socketio

It adds the package, the provider, the config and the env key (steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 below). It never overwrites a file, so it is safe to run twice. Then write a namespace (step 4) and connect a client (step 6). Add --broadcasting to also turn on broadcasting.

docs.title: Set it up by hand
docs.text: If you do not use dox add socketio, do all the steps below.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text: dart pub add dox_socketio

docs.title: 2. The provider
docs.text:
The provider starts Socket.IO in every isolate. Put it in lib/providers/, so the generated container finds it:

lib/providers/socketio_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/socketio.dart';

class AppSocketIoProvider extends SocketIoProvider {
  AppSocketIoProvider() : super(socketIoConfig);
}

docs.title: 3. The config
docs.text:
The config says which namespaces to serve:

lib/config/socketio.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
);
SocketIoConfig option Default What it does enabled true serve Socket.IO at options.path options ServerOptions() see Options namespaces [] NamespaceHandler classes to register adapter null makes one adapter in each isolate, see Many isolates

docs.title: 4. A namespace
docs.text:
A namespace handles the events of one path, like /chat:

lib/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.emit('welcome', <String, dynamic>{'id': socket.id});
    socket.join('lobby');
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.socket.to('lobby').emit('message', event.data); // everyone in lobby but me
    event.ack('sent'); // answer the client callback
  }
}

docs.title: 5. Turn it on
docs.text:
Add a getter for the SOCKETIO_ENABLED key to lib/config/env.dart:

lib/config/env.dart
  /// serve Socket.IO on the app port
  bool get socketioEnabled => false;
.env
SOCKETIO_ENABLED=true

Then run dart run build_runner build and dox serve.

docs.title: 6. Connect a client
docs.text:
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', { transports: ['websocket'] });
socket.on('welcome', (data) => console.log(data.id));
socket.emit('message', 'hi', (answer) => console.log(answer)); // 'sent'

Use transports: ['websocket'], because long-polling does not work with many isolates. See Many isolates.

Requests to /socket.io/ go to Socket.IO before the router, so route middleware does not run for them. To log users in, see Log in a socket.

docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text:
A namespace is a class, so its dependencies come in through the constructor:

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  ChatNamespace(this.messages);

  final MessageService messages;

  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.ack(messages.save(event.data));
  }
}

// in lib/config/socketio.dart
namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace(MessageService())],

docs.title: Namespace middleware
docs.text:
Sometimes you want to check a client before it joins. Add a middleware to the namespace. When it throws a SocketIoException, the client gets connect_error with the message and the data:

@override
List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[checkToken];

void checkToken(Socket socket) {
  if (socket.handshake.auth['token'] != 'secret') {
    throw SocketIoException('unauthorized', data: <String, dynamic>{'reason': 'bad token'});
  }
}

Any other error is written to stderr, and the client only gets {"message": "Internal error"}. So private text, like SQL, never reaches the client.

docs.title: Sending from a controller or a service
docs.text:
SocketIoProvider.server is the Socket.IO server of this isolate:

await SocketIoProvider.server?.of('/chat').to('lobby').emit('news', data);

From a queue job or another program, use the emitter.

docs.title: Common methods
docs.text:
The API follows the Node.js server. This table shows the few places where Dart is different:

Node.js Dart socket.on('e', (a, cb) => ...) socket.on('e', (SocketEvent e) => ...), then e.data, e.args, e.ack(x) socket.emit('e', a, b) socket.emit('e', a) or socket.emitArgs('e', [a, b]) await socket.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a) await socket.emitWithAck('e', a, timeout: Duration(seconds: 5)) socket.join(r) / socket.leave(r) the same socket.to(r).emit(...) the same socket.broadcast.emit(...) the same io.to(r).except(x).emit(...) the same io.of('/chat'), io.use(fn) the same socket.handshake .headers, .query, .auth, .address, .token, .cookie(name), .session() socket.data socket.data (a Map) await io.in(r).fetchSockets() await io.to(r).fetchSockets() (all servers) await io.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a) await io.timeout(Duration(seconds: 5)).emitWithAck('e', a) io.serverSideEmit('e', a) await io.serverSideEmit('e', [a]) io.on('e', (a, cb) => ...) (from other servers) io.onServerSideEmit('e', (ServerSideEvent e) => ...), then e.data, e.ack(x)

To send binary data, send a Uint8List. It can be anywhere in lists and maps. The disconnecting and disconnect events give the reason in event.data, like transport close.

docs.title: Log in a socket
docs.text:
Socket.IO gets its requests before the router, so route middleware like session and auth does not run. Use SocketAuth as a namespace middleware instead. Your function gets the handshake and returns the user, or null:

lib/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart
class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[SocketAuth(findUser).handle];

  static Future<User?> findUser(Handshake handshake) async {
    String? token = handshake.token;
    if (token == null) return null;
    return User().where('api_token', token).getFirst();
  }

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    User user = socket.user! as User;
    socket.join('user:${user.id}');
  }
}

The client sends the token in auth. Browsers can not set headers on a websocket, so use auth and not a header:

const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', {
  transports: ['websocket'],
  auth: { token: 'the-user-token' },
});
socket.on('connect_error', (err) => console.log(err.message)); // 'Unauthorized'

When the function returns a user, it is kept in socket.user. When it returns null, the client gets a connect_error with the message Unauthorized, and onConnection does not run.

The handshake gives you these helpers:

  • handshake.token is auth.token from the client, else the Authorization: Bearer header.
  • handshake.cookie('name') reads a cookie and decrypts it with the APP_KEY. Use decrypt: false for a plain cookie.
  • await handshake.session() gives the Dox session of the client, from its session cookie.

docs.title: With dox_auth
docs.text:
dox_auth can check a JWT or the web login session for you:

static Future<User?> findUser(Handshake handshake) async {
  // an API client or a mobile app sends a JWT
  String? token = handshake.token;
  if (token != null) return Auth(guard: 'api').userFromToken(token);

  // a browser that logged in on a web page sends the session cookie
  Session session = await handshake.session();
  return Auth(guard: 'web').userFromSession(session);
}

userFromToken runs the same checks as AuthMiddleware, so a bad, expired or revoked token gives null. handshake.session() runs the same checks as SessionMiddleware.

The session is read once, when the socket connects. A logout later does not close the socket, so call socket.disconnect() yourself if you need that.

Cookie login needs allowedOrigins

A browser sends its cookies on a websocket from any website. So if you log users in with a cookie, set allowedOrigins to your own sites. Without it, another website can open a socket as your user.

docs.title: Many isolates
docs.text:
Dox runs one isolate per CPU core, and each isolate has its own Socket.IO server. A client is connected to one of them.

With many isolates, the provider uses the IsolateAdapter by default. It sends each broadcast to the other isolates of the process, so it reaches every client. socketsJoin, fetchSockets, serverSideEmit and broadcast acks work across isolates too. You need no Redis for this.

Adapter Reaches InMemoryAdapter (one isolate) the clients of this isolate IsolateAdapter (many isolates, the default) the clients of every isolate of this process RedisAdapter the clients of every isolate of every server

Clients should connect with websocket only. One websocket stays on one isolate, but long-polling sends many requests that can reach different isolates. Long-polling only works with totalIsolate: 1, or with sticky sessions in front of many single-isolate servers.

Add each namespace in the config, so it is added in every isolate. A namespace that only one isolate adds with io.of('/x') gets no answer from the others, so fetchSockets and serverSideEmitWithAck wait 5 seconds and throw.

docs.title: Many servers: Redis adapter
docs.text:
If you run more than one server process, or Dox next to Node.js servers, use the Redis adapter. Then a broadcast on one server reaches the clients of all servers.

Add the ioredis package:

dart pub add ioredis

Then make the adapter in each isolate with a factory, because a Redis connection can not be sent to another isolate:

lib/config/socketio.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
  adapter: const RedisSocketAdapterFactory(),
);

/// makes the Redis adapter inside each isolate.
/// A Redis connection can not be sent to another isolate.
class RedisSocketAdapterFactory extends SocketAdapterFactory {
  const RedisSocketAdapterFactory();

  @override
  Adapter create() {
    Redis redis = Redis(); // 127.0.0.1:6379. Or Redis(RedisOptions(host: ..., port: ...))
    return RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis);
  }
}

The subscriber needs its own connection, because a Redis connection in subscribe mode can not run other commands.

The adapter uses the format of @socket.io/redis-adapter, so Node.js servers with that adapter can share one Redis with Dox servers. If your Node.js servers use a JSON parser, set format: RedisFormat.json.

docs.title: Acting on all servers
docs.text:
With the Redis adapter, these methods work on the sockets of all servers:

// sockets of every server. Sockets of this server are `Socket`s.
List<RemoteSocket> sockets = await io.to('room1').fetchSockets();
for (RemoteSocket socket in sockets) {
  socket.emit('hello', socket.data['name']);
}

await io.to('room1').socketsJoin('room2');
await io.to('banned').disconnectSockets();

To get one ack from each client on all servers, set a timeout:

List<Object?> answers = await io
    .timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))
    .emitWithAck('ping', 'are you there?');

fetchSockets throws a TimeoutException when a server does not answer within requestsTimeout (5 seconds by default).

docs.title: Events between servers
docs.text:
Sometimes the servers need to tell each other something, like "reload the config". serverSideEmit sends an event to the other servers. Clients do not get it:

// on every server
io.onServerSideEmit('reload-config', (ServerSideEvent event) {
  reloadConfig(event.data);
  event.ack('done'); // only when the sender waits for an answer
});

// on one server
await io.serverSideEmit('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);

To wait for one answer from each other server, use serverSideEmitWithAck. When a server does not answer in time, it throws an AckTimeoutException, and its responses holds the answers that came back:

List<Object?> answers = await io.serverSideEmitWithAck('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);

docs.title: Emit from other programs
docs.text:
Sometimes you want to send an event from a queue worker, a cron job or a service in another language. An emitter does this without a Socket.IO server. It writes to Redis, and every server with the Redis adapter sends the event to its clients:

import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
  SocketIoEmitter emitter = SocketIoEmitter(redis);

  await emitter.emit('news', <String, dynamic>{'title': 'hello'}); // all clients of `/`
  await emitter.to('room1').except('room2').emit('news', 'hi room1');
  await emitter.of('/chat').to('vip').emit('notice', 'for vip');

  await emitter.to('room1').socketsJoin('room3'); // sockets in room1 join room3
  await emitter.to('room3').socketsLeave('room1');
  await emitter.to('banned').disconnectSockets();

  await redis.disconnect();
}

The emitter does not wait for an answer, so it can not know if a client got the event.

The emitters of other languages use the same format, so they work too. For example, Node.js with @socket.io/redis-emitter:

import { Emitter } from '@socket.io/redis-emitter';
import { createClient } from 'redis';

const redis = createClient({ url: 'redis://127.0.0.1:6379' });
await redis.connect();

const emitter = new Emitter(redis);
emitter.to('room1').emit('news', { title: 'hello' });
emitter.of('/chat').emit('notice', 'for everyone in /chat');

docs.title: Broadcasting
docs.text: To send events to public, private and presence channels, see Broadcasting.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Pass ServerOptions as options to SocketIoConfig in a Dox app, or to SocketIoServer without Dox:

SocketIoServer(
  options: ServerOptions(
    path: '/socket.io/',
    pingInterval: Duration(seconds: 25),
    pingTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
    maxHttpBufferSize: 1000000,
    transports: <String>['polling', 'websocket'],
    cors: CorsOptions(origins: <String>['https://my.app'], credentials: true),
  ),
);
Option Default What it does path /socket.io/ the URL path pingInterval 25 s how often the server sends a ping pingTimeout 20 s how long to wait for the pong before the client is gone upgradeTimeout 10 s how long an upgrade from polling to websocket may take connectTimeout 45 s how long the client has to join a namespace maxHttpBufferSize 1,000,000 bytes the biggest message. A bigger websocket message closes the connection maxAttachments 10 the most binary parts in one packet transports ['polling', 'websocket'] allowed transports allowUpgrades true let polling clients move to websocket cors null CORS headers for polling requests. With a list of origins, it also checks the origin of websockets allowedOrigins null the sites that may connect, see Allowed origins allowRequest null accepts or refuses each request, see Allow requests and limit sessions maxSessions null the most open sessions per isolate. Set it in production maxAttachmentBytes null the most bytes of all binary parts of one packet. A bigger packet closes the client maxAuthSize null the most bytes of the auth payload of a connect. A bigger one gets connect_error (auth payload too large) maxWriteBufferSize null the most bytes kept for a client that does not read, like a polling client that stopped. Above it, the session closes ackTimeout null the default timeout of emitWithAck. With null, it waits until the client answers or leaves

docs.title: Waiting for acks
docs.text:
socket.waitingAcks is the number of acks a socket still waits for. Use it to see a client that never answers:

int waiting = socket.waitingAcks;

docs.title: Allowed origins
docs.text:
allowedOrigins says which websites may open a socket. You should set it when you log users in with cookies:

ServerOptions(allowedOrigins: <String>['https://app.example.com']);
  • null (the default): no extra check. Dox logs a warning at start.
  • []: only pages of the same host can connect.
  • A list of sites: the same host and those sites can connect.
  • ['*']: every site can connect.

Other sites get 403. A client with no Origin header (not a browser) is always allowed.

docs.title: Allow requests and limit sessions
docs.text:
allowRequest runs for every handshake and every websocket upgrade. It gets an EngineRequest with the headers, query and address, and returns true or false. maxSessions is the most open sessions:

lib/config/socketio.dart
SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  options: ServerOptions(
    allowRequest: (EngineRequest req) => req.query['key'] == 'secret',
    maxSessions: 10000,
  ),
);

When allowRequest gives false or throws, the client gets 403. At the limit, a new handshake gets 503 and open sessions keep working. The count is per isolate, so with 4 isolates the app allows 4 times maxSessions. Without maxSessions, every GET request makes a session that lives about 45 seconds, so Dox logs one warning at start.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dox_socketio also runs on its own, with no Dox app:

import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer();
  io.register(ChatNamespace());
  await io.listen(3001);
}
  • io.listen(port) starts a native server on its own port. Run it in its own small program, like bin/socket.dart, behind the same proxy as the HTTP server.
  • io.attach(httpServer) uses a server you already have: a NativeHttpServer or a dart:io one.
  • In your own server, call io.handle(request) when io.matches(request) is true.
  • io.on('connection', (Socket socket) {...}) handles the default namespace / with no class.
  • io.use(SocketAuth(findUser).handle) logs users in on the default namespace.

To use the Redis adapter, pass it to the server:

Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer(
  adapter: RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis),
);

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
• With no provider, or with enabled: false, there is no extra work per request.
  • Need a plain WebSocket with no Socket.IO protocol? Route.websocket(path, handler) in dox_core gives you the raw socket.
  • Dox logs a hint at startup when it runs many isolates and polling is allowed.
  • A client that a middleware refuses is closed after connectTimeout, unless it joins another namespace.
  • socket.user stays on this server. fetchSockets() on other servers does not get it.
  • SocketAuth(findUser, message: '...') changes the Unauthorized message.
  • handshake.session() uses AppConfig.session. Pass another SessionConfig like handshake.session(config). The session is read only, so changes are not saved. It prints a warning once when allowedOrigins is null or has '*'.
  • With userCacheTtl on in dox_auth, a deleted or banned user can still connect until the cache time ends, unless forgetUser runs.
  • With the cookie session driver, an old copy of the session cookie still works after logout until the lifetime ends. Use the cache driver if a logout must stop old cookies.
  • cors with * in origins, or cors: null, allows websockets from any origin. * with credentials: true throws an ArgumentError.
  • Websocket compression is off. A message bigger than maxHttpBufferSize closes with code 1009. On a plain dart:io server, the whole message is read before the size check, so also set a size limit in your proxy.
  • A packet with more than maxAttachments binary parts closes that client.
  • allowRequest does not run again for the polling requests of an open session. A client that leaves while it runs still holds a maxSessions slot until the ping timeout. A browser client only sees a connect error, not the 403 or 503 body.
  • The Redis adapter reads msgpack and JSON, and writes msgpack. Long-polling with it needs sticky sessions too.
  • The emitter key must be the same as the adapter key. Both default to socket.io. Binary data (Uint8List, or Buffer in Node.js) arrives as binary.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
dox_storage saves and reads files with one API, on the local disk, AWS S3 and S3-compatible services.

You write the same code for every place. Only the config decides where the files go. This page shows the full API of a disk. For a shorter guide, see File Storage.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
A new app from dox create already has this setup. You can go to Using a disk.

First, install the package:

dart pub add dox_storage

Then add the config. Each disk has a name and a driver:

lib/config/storage.dart
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

StorageConfig storageConfig = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: env.storageDisk, // STORAGE_DISK in .env, default 'local'
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'local': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'},
  },
);

Last, add the provider. It sets up the disks in every isolate. Put it in lib/providers/, so the generated container finds it:

lib/providers/storage_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/storage.dart';

class AppStorageProvider extends StorageProvider {
  AppStorageProvider() : super(storageConfig);
}

Then run dart run build_runner build.

S3 disks and their env keys are in File Storage.

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text: Driver Use for Signed download URL Signed upload URL local a folder on the server Yes (HMAC with your app key) No s3 AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, GCS (HMAC keys) Yes (SigV4) Yes (SigV4) memory tests fake URLs fake URLs

docs.title: Using a disk
docs.text:
Storage() has short functions for common work. For example, putFile saves an upload with a new random name:

Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  String path = await Storage().putFile('avatars', file);
  return <String, String>{'path': path}; // /avatars/<uuid>.png
});

For the full API, get a Disk with use. With no name, you get the default disk:

Disk disk = Storage().use('s3');

The rest of this page shows the methods of a Disk.

docs.title: Storing files
docs.text:
The put method stores a String, a List<int> or a Stream<List<int>>:

await disk.put('avatars/1.png', bytes);

You can set the content type and the visibility with WriteOptions:

await disk.put('a.json', '{}', options: WriteOptions(contentType: 'application/json', visibility: Visibility.public));

docs.title: Storing big files
docs.text:
putStream writes a stream, so the file is not loaded into memory:

await disk.putStream('videos/big.mp4', File('big.mp4').openRead());

docs.title: Saving an upload
docs.text:
Stream the upload to the disk, so the file is not loaded into memory:

Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  String key = 'avatars/${DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch}.${file.extension}';
  await disk.putStream(key, file.stream());
  return <String, String>{'url': await disk.getUrl(key)};
});

Do not use file.filename from the client as the key, because a client can send any name. Make your own name, like above or with a uuid.

docs.title: Adding to a file
docs.text:
append adds text at the end of a file, and prepend adds it at the start. A missing file is made:

await disk.append('logs/app.log', 'new line');

await disk.prepend('logs/app.log', 'first line');

They put a \n between the old and the new text, if the file is not empty. Change it with separator, like separator: ', '. They read the file and write it back, so two writers at the same time can lose a write.

docs.title: Retrieving files
docs.text:
get reads a file as bytes, and getString reads it as text:

Uint8List data = await disk.get('avatars/1.png');

String text = await disk.getString('notes/a.txt');

For a big file, use getStream:

Stream<List<int>> stream = await disk.getStream('videos/big.mp4');

docs.title: Checking if a file exists
docs.text:
exists returns true when the file is there. missing is the opposite:

bool found = await disk.exists('avatars/1.png');

bool gone = await disk.missing('c.png');

docs.title: File metadata
docs.text:
getMetaData gives the size, content type, last change time and etag in one call. size and lastModified give one value each:

ObjectMetaData meta = await disk.getMetaData('avatars/1.png');

int size = await disk.size('avatars/1.png');

DateTime changed = await disk.lastModified('avatars/1.png');

size and lastModified throw FileNotFoundException when the file is missing.

docs.title: Copying and moving files
docs.text:
await disk.copy('a.png', 'b.png');

await disk.move('b.png', 'c.png');

On S3, copy and move copy on the server, so the file does not pass through your app.

docs.title: Deleting files
docs.text:
delete removes one file. deleteAll removes every file under a prefix:

await disk.delete('c.png');

await disk.deleteAll('avatars'); // '' or no argument for the whole disk

docs.title: Directories
docs.text:
files gives the files directly in a folder, and allFiles also gives the files in sub folders. directories gives the direct sub folders. They return keys, like avatars/1.png:

List<String> files = await disk.files('avatars');

List<String> all = await disk.allFiles('avatars');

List<String> folders = await disk.directories('avatars');

deleteDirectory deletes a folder and its files. It never deletes the root, so '' or / throws InvalidKeyException:

await disk.deleteDirectory('reports');

makeDirectory makes a folder and its parents on a local disk. On other disks it does nothing, because they have no real folders. directoryExists checks a folder. On S3 and memory disks, a folder exists when a file is under it:

await disk.makeDirectory('reports/2026');

bool folder = await disk.directoryExists('reports');

docs.title: Listing page by page
docs.text:
For a big folder, read it one page at a time with listAll:

ListResult page = await disk.listAll('avatars', ListOptions(recursive: true, limit: 100));
// next page: ListOptions(paginationToken: page.paginationToken)

docs.title: File visibility
docs.text:
A file is public or private. Set it with setVisibility, and read it with getVisibility:

await disk.setVisibility('avatars/1.png', Visibility.public);

Visibility v = await disk.getVisibility('avatars/1.png');

On a local disk, visibility does nothing by default. To make it set real file modes, turn on file permissions.

docs.title: URLs
docs.text:
getUrl gives the address of a file. Set url on the disk to serve public files from a CDN:

String url = await disk.getUrl('avatars/1.png');

docs.title: Signed URLs
docs.text:
A signed URL works only for a short time, so you can share a private file. expiresIn is 30 minutes when you do not set it:

String signed = await disk.getSignedUrl('avatars/1.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10)));

contentDisposition asks the server to send this header on download, like attachment; filename="report.pdf". On S3, a signed URL can live at most 7 days.

On a local disk, the app serves the file itself. Storage.route('files') adds a route that checks the signature and serves the file.

docs.title: Signed upload URLs
docs.text:
On S3, the browser can upload a file straight to the bucket with a signed upload URL. So the file does not pass through your app:

String upload = await disk.getSignedUploadUrl('avatars/2.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(contentType: 'image/png'));

docs.title: Atomic writes
docs.text:
Sometimes an upload fails or stops in the middle. Turn on atomic_writes so this never leaves a half written file. The disk then writes to a temp file and renames it when the write is done, so the old file stays until then:

'local': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage', 'atomic_writes': true},

It is off by default.

docs.title: Local file permissions
docs.text:
Turn on permissions if you want visibility to set the real file mode. Then setVisibility runs chmod and getVisibility reads the mode:

'local': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage', 'permissions': true},

The modes are 0644 for a public file, 0600 for a private file, 0755 for a public folder and 0700 for a private folder. To use other modes, give a map instead of true:

'permissions': <String, dynamic>{
  'file': <String, int>{'public': 0x1a4, 'private': 0x180},
  'dir': <String, int>{'public': 0x1ed, 'private': 0x1c0},
},

A mode that is not in the map keeps its default. Each mode must be an int from 0 to 0x1ff (0777). It is off by default, and it does nothing on Windows.

docs.title: S3-compatible services
docs.text:
The examples use S3DriverConfig, the class behind an s3 disk. In a Dox config, the same settings are keys in the disk map. See File Storage.

Two more fields have defaults. multipartPartSize is the size of one part of a big upload (8 MiB). unsignedPayload skips the hash of the body (false). Only turn it on over HTTPS.

docs.title: Cloudflare R2
docs.text:
Set supportsAcl: false, because R2 does not take ACL headers:

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'auto',
  endpoint: 'https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com',
  accessKeyId: '...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
  supportsAcl: false,
);

docs.title: MinIO
docs.text:
MinIO needs path style URLs, so set forcePathStyle: true:

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'us-east-1',
  endpoint: 'http://localhost:9000',
  forcePathStyle: true,
  accessKeyId: 'minioadmin',
  secretAccessKey: 'minioadmin',
);

docs.title: DigitalOcean Spaces
docs.text:
Spaces works like S3. Put the region of your space in region and in the endpoint:

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-space',
  region: 'nyc3',
  endpoint: 'https://nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com',
  accessKeyId: '...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
);

docs.title: Google Cloud Storage
docs.text:
Set supportsAcl: false and supportsBatchDelete: false, because GCS does not take ACL headers or the S3 batch delete call:

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'auto',
  endpoint: 'https://storage.googleapis.com',
  accessKeyId: 'GOOG...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
  supportsAcl: false,
  supportsBatchDelete: false,
);

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
fake() swaps a disk for a memory disk, so your tests write nothing to the real disk. In a Dox app, the DriveManager is Storage.manager:

Disk fake = drive.fake('s3'); // drive.use('s3') now writes to memory
await uploadAvatar();         // your code
expect(await fake.exists('avatars/1.png'), isTrue);
drive.restore('s3');

A disk also has assertExists and assertMissing. They throw a StateError when the check fails:

await fake.assertExists('avatars/1.png');

await fake.assertMissing('avatars/old.png');

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All errors extend StorageException and have the key.

Error When FileNotFoundException the file does not exist PermissionDeniedException file system permission error, or S3 403 InvalidKeyException unsafe key UnsupportedOperationException the driver can not do this DriverException anything else. The first error is in cause

Keys are checked, so a user can not reach files outside the disk. .., absolute paths like /etc/passwd and null bytes throw InvalidKeyException. A local disk also checks that the path stays inside its root folder.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dox_storage also works on its own:

dart pub add dox_storage

Make a DriveManager with your disks:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

Map<String, String> env = Platform.environment;

DriveManager drive = DriveManager(
  defaultDisk: 'local',
  disks: <String, DriverContract>{
    'local': LocalDriver(LocalDriverConfig(
      root: 'storage',
      urlBase: 'https://app.test/uploads',
      atomicWrites: true, // off by default
      appKey: env['APP_KEY'], // signs local URLs
    )),
    's3': S3Driver(S3DriverConfig(
      bucket: 'my-bucket',
      region: 'us-east-1',
      accessKeyId: env['AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID']!,
      secretAccessKey: env['AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY']!,
    )),
  },
);

Disk disk = drive.use('s3'); // or drive.use() for the default disk

use() throws UnsupportedOperationException when no disk has that name. For file permissions, pass LocalDriverConfig(permissions: LocalPermissions()).

docs.title: Checking a local signed URL
docs.text:
A local signed URL looks like <urlBase>/<key>?expires=...&signature=.... Without Dox, check it in the route that serves the file:

LocalDriver local = LocalDriver(localConfig);
bool ok = local.verifySignedUrl(keyFromPath, req.uri.queryParameters);
if (!ok) {
  return response('Forbidden').statusCode(403);
}

docs.title: Your own driver
docs.text:
Implement DriverContract and register it:

class DropboxDriver implements DriverContract { ... }

drive.register('dropbox', DropboxDriver(...));
await drive.use('dropbox').put('a.txt', 'hello');

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
This section is for special cases. Most apps do not need it.

  • Keys are cleaned: a//b/./c.txt becomes a/b/c.txt, and \ becomes /.
  • append and prepend keep the visibility and the content type of the file.
  • On local disks, copy or move of a missing file throws FileNotFoundException and makes no folders.
  • Atomic writes use temp files that end with .dox-upload.tmp. listAll() hides them.
  • On S3, put sends one request, so it allows at most 5 GiB. putStream uses a multipart upload when the stream is bigger than multipartPartSize (8 MiB). Only one part is in memory at a time, and the limit is about 78 GiB. Raise multipartPartSize for bigger files. copy and move also allow at most 5 GiB.
  • Without permissions, setVisibility on a local disk does nothing, and getVisibility gives the disk visibility.
  • With permissions:
    • The mode is set before the content is written, so a private file is never readable by others, not even for a moment.
    • A new file gets the visibility of the write, or the disk visibility. An overwrite, append, prepend and move keep the mode of the file, unless the call gives a visibility. A copy gets the visibility of the call, or the mode of the source.
    • Folders that a write creates get the folder mode. Folders that were there before, and the disk root, keep their mode.
    • getVisibility reads the real mode: the private mode is private, any other mode is public.
    • getVisibility and setVisibility of a symlink throw UnsupportedOperationException. A copy onto a symlink replaces the link.
    • When chmod fails, a file that the write created is removed.
    • A mode that is not an int, like '0644', or is out of range throws ArgumentError when the disk is made. A key in the map that is not file, dir, public or private is ignored.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
dox_validation checks input and gives you typed Dart objects.

It has two parts:

  1. DTOs: a class with @Dto() and rule annotations. A generator writes the checks. Use this for almost everything. See DTOs.
  2. Fluent schemas: v.object(...). Use them only when you know the shape of the input at runtime, not when you write the code.

Both give all errors at once, and both give a JSON Schema for OpenAPI.

docs.title: In a Dox app
docs.text:
dox_core uses dox_validation and exports it, so there is nothing to install. import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' is all you need.

  1. Make a DTO with dox make:dto CreateUser. It writes lib/app/dtos/create_user/create_user.dto.dart.
  2. Run the generator: dox build_runner:build.
  3. Give the list of DTOs to the app, once:
lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:my_app/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  dtos: dtos, // from lib/generated/dtos.g.dart
);

Then ask for the DTO in a controller. Dox checks the body before the method runs. Bad input gets 422 with the errors:

lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart
class UserController {
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> store(CreateUser body) async {
    // body is already checked and typed
    return <String, dynamic>{'name': body.name};
  }
}

The full guide is at Validation. Every rule is in the rules reference. The rest of this page is about the package itself.

docs.title: Defining a DTO
docs.text:
A DTO is a class with @Dto(). Each field gets its rules as annotations:

import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  @Trim()
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  const CreateUser({required this.name, required this.email});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}

For each @Dto class, the generator writes a const DtoSchema<CreateUser> named $CreateUserDto. It holds the checks, the converter and the JSON Schema. The static const schema line lets you reach it as CreateUser.schema.

The generator also writes lib/generated/dtos.g.dart, with a list dtos of every DTO in lib/. Dox uses it to find a DTO by its type.

docs.title: Validating a map
docs.text: DtoSchema<T> is also a normal Schema<T>. So you can use it inside v.object(...) and v.list(...), and with OpenAPI.

docs.title: Validating and throwing
docs.text:
Use validateMap to run all checks and get the object. It throws a ValidationException with the errors when the input is not valid:

CreateUser user = await CreateUser.schema.validateMap(input);

docs.title: Validating without throwing
docs.text:
Use safeValidateMap when you want to handle the errors yourself. It never throws for bad input:

ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(input);
if (!result.success) {
  print(result.errors); // {'email': 'The email is not a valid email'}
}

A ParseResult has:

  • success: true when there are no errors.
  • value: the result, or null when success is false.
  • errors: the first message for each field, like {'user.email': '...'}.
  • fieldErrors: all messages for each field.
  • issues: the full list of ValidationIssue objects, with code and path.

Both methods take these options:

  • source: Source.query reads the map like a query string, so text is converted to the field type.
  • params are the path params. @Unique(ignoreParam: ...) uses them.
  • messages and locale change the error text for this call. See Messages.

dox_core has its own ValidationException (the HTTP 422 one), so it does not export the one from dox_validation. In a controller, both answer 422. In tests, use safeValidateMap.

docs.title: Building an object with no checks
docs.text:
fromMap builds the object with no checks. It reads the keys, converts JSON types and fills in defaults. Use it only for data you trust, because a wrong type throws a TypeError:

CreateUser user = CreateUser.schema.fromMap(trustedData);

docs.title: Turning an object back into a map
docs.text:
toMap gives the object as a map with the input keys (snake_case). A DateTime becomes an ISO 8601 string and an enum becomes its name:

Map<String, dynamic> data = CreateUser.schema.toMap(user);

docs.title: Getting the JSON Schema
docs.text:
toJsonSchema gives the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the DTO:

CreateUser.schema.toJsonSchema();

For a CreateUser with age and role fields, you get:

{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "CreateUser",
  "properties": {
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 3, "maxLength": 50 },
    "email": { "type": "string", "format": "email" },
    "age": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 18 },
    "role": { "type": "string", "enum": ["admin", "user"], "default": "user" }
  },
  "required": ["name", "email"]
}

A /// doc comment on a field becomes its description. @Describe('...') on a field also sets it, and wins over the comment. Each rule adds its own keys, see the rules reference.

docs.title: Fluent schemas (for dynamic input)
docs.text:
Sometimes you only know the fields at runtime. Then use a fluent schema. The output is a Map, not a class:

final ObjectSchema createUser = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'name': v.string().trim().min(3).max(50),
  'email': v.string().email(),
  'age': v.coerce.int().min(18).optional(),
  'role': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['admin', 'user']).defaultTo('user'),
  'tags': v.list(v.string()).max(5),
  'address': Address.schema, // a DTO inside a fluent schema
});

Use parse to get the data. It throws a ValidationException when the input is not valid:

Map<String, dynamic> data = createUser.parse(input);

Use safeParse if you do not want it to throw:

ParseResult<Map<String, dynamic>> result = createUser.safeParse(input);

In a controller, use req.validateSchema:

Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(createUser);

Fluent schemas do not follow the DTO defaults, so watch out:

  • A key is required unless you add optional().
  • "" is a value, not "missing".
  • Text is not converted to numbers or booleans, unless you use v.coerce.

docs.title: Available schemas
docs.text: Schema Checks v.string() min, max, length, nonEmpty, email, url, uuid, ip, datetime, regex, startsWith, endsWith, includes, alpha, alphaDash, alphaNumeric, json, digits, digitsBetween, dateFormat, password, exists, unique, trim, toLowerCase, toUpperCase v.int(), v.num() min, max, between, gt, lt, positive, nonNegative, multipleOf, exists, unique v.bool() v.date() DateTime only. min, max v.enumOf([...]), v.literal(x) v.list(item) min, max, nonEmpty v.object({...}) strict, passthrough, strip, pick, omit, extend, partial v.map(values, keys: ...) any keys v.union([...]) the first match wins v.any(), v.file() file() has maxSize, minSize, mimes, mimeTypes, dimensions, image and extensions

docs.title: Optional and nullable values
docs.text:
Every schema has these methods:

  • optional(): the key may be missing. null is still an error.
  • nullable(): the value may be null, but the key must be there.
  • nullish(): both.
  • defaultTo(x): the value when the key is missing. (default is a reserved word in Dart.)
v.string().optional();
v.int().defaultTo(0);

Every schema also has transform, refine, superRefine, use(rule), same(other), confirmed(), and describe(text) and example(x) for the JSON Schema.

docs.title: Converting text
docs.text:
Query strings and form data are always text. v.coerce turns the text into the right type first:

v.coerce.int().parse('42');       // 42
v.coerce.num().parse('4.5');      // 4.5
v.coerce.bool().parse('on');      // true (true/1/yes/on, false/0/no/off)
v.coerce.date().parse('2024-01-31');
v.coerce.string().parse(5);       // '5'

docs.title: Checking across fields
docs.text:
If a rule needs two fields, use refine on the object. path says which field gets the error:

final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'password': v.string().min(8),
  'confirm': v.string(),
}).refine((Map<String, dynamic> data) {
  return data['password'] == data['confirm'];
}, message: 'Passwords do not match', path: <Object>['confirm']);

docs.title: More rules
docs.text:
Fluent schemas have the same rules as the DTO annotations, with the same codes and messages:

final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  // needs password_confirmation with the same value
  'password': v.string().password(min: 8, mixedCase: true, numbers: true).confirmed(),
  'email': v.string().email().unique('users', column: 'email'),
  'team_id': v.int().exists('teams'),
  'type': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['person', 'company']),
  'company': v.string().optional().requiredIf('type', 'company'),
  'phone': v.string().digitsBetween(8, 12).optional(),
  'country_code': v.string().optional().requiredWith(<String>['phone']),
  'birthday': v.string().dateFormat('Y-m-d').optional(),
  'settings': v.string().json().optional(),
  'age': v.int().between(18, 120).optional(),
});

Map<String, dynamic> data = await signUp.parseAsync(input);

There are more presence and compare rules:

final ObjectSchema order = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'type': v.string(),
  'email': v.string().optional().requiredWithout(<String>['phone']),
  'phone': v.string().optional(),
  'fax': v.string().optional().requiredWithoutAll(<String>['email', 'phone']),
  'company': v.string().optional().requiredUnless('type', 'person'),
  'nick': v.string().optional().filled(),
  'note': v.string().optional().present().nullable(),
  'coupon': v.string().optional().prohibitedIf('type', 'guest'),
  'debug': v.any().optional().prohibited(),
  'terms': v.coerce.bool().accepted(),
  'new_password': v.string().different('old_password'),
  'id': v.string().ulid(),
  'min_price': v.int(),
  'max_price': v.int().gtField('min_price'),
});

Each rule is explained in the rules reference. Keep these points in mind:

  • The required..., prohibited..., filled and present rules come after optional() (or nullish()).
  • exists and unique ask the database, so they are async. Use parseAsync() or safeParseAsync().
  • exists(table, column: 'id'): the column default is id. Use v.int().exists('teams') for a number id, so text like abc fails before any query.
  • unique(table, column: 'email', ignore: id): column is required. ignore skips the row with this id, so you can use it for updates.
  • accepted() on v.bool() takes only true. For form words like yes and on, use v.coerce.bool().accepted().

docs.title: Stop at the first error
docs.text:
A fluent schema runs all rules of a value, and gives one error for each failed rule. If you want only the first error, add .bail(). A DTO always does this.

v.string().min(8).email().bail().safeParse('ab');
// one error: min_length. Without bail(): min_length and email.

Put .bail() before .optional(), .nullable() or .transform(), because rules after them belong to the wrapper. Async rules after a failed rule do not run, so no query is made for a value that is already wrong.

docs.title: Skip a field
docs.text:
Sometimes a field only matters for some input. excludeIf(other, value) and excludeUnless(other, value) skip a field of v.object(). When they match, the field is not checked and its key is not in the output:

final ObjectSchema account = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'type': v.string(),
  'vat_number': v.string().min(5).excludeIf('type', 'person'),
  'company': v.string().excludeUnless('type', 'company'),
});

account.parse(<String, dynamic>{'type': 'person', 'vat_number': 'x'});
// {type: person}

other must be a key of the same object. A skipped field never gets its default.

docs.title: Async checks
docs.text:
If a check needs the database, use refineAsync. Then call parseAsync() or safeParseAsync(), because parse() throws a StateError when a schema has async checks:

v.string().refineAsync(isFreeName, message: 'The name is taken');

docs.title: Custom rules
docs.text:
A Rule<T> class works in both places: as an annotation on a DTO, and with use() in a fluent schema:

v.string().min(3).use(const Slug());

See Custom rules for how to write one.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Each error has a code, like required or min_length. A message can use placeholders: {field}, {value}, and rule values like {min} and {max}.

To change messages for the whole app, set MessageResolver.global. In a Dox app, use AppConfig(validationMessages: ...) instead:

MessageResolver.global = MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'required': 'Please fill in {field}',
});

To change messages for one call, pass messages. It replaces the global resolver for that call:

createUser.safeParse(input, messages: MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
}));

To show a nice name for {field} instead of the key, give attributes:

MessageResolver.global = MessageResolver(
  attributes: <String, String>{'first_name': 'first name'},
);
// The first name is required

A DTO can give its own names with @Dto(attributes:). For other languages, extend MessageResolver and override resolve(). See Messages.

docs.title: Opt-in flags
docs.text:
ValidationFlags turns on behaviors that are off by default. Set it in Validator.flags:

// turn on one flag
Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags(unicodeAlpha: true);

// turn on every flag
Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags.all();

Each isolate has its own Validator.flags. So in a Dox app, set it in a provider's setup(), which runs in every isolate:

class ValidationProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags.all();
  }
}
Flag What it does when on emptyStringsToNull Fluent schemas turn each "" into null before the check, also in nested maps and lists. A DTO checked on its own keeps ""; use @Dto(emptyStringsToNull: true) there. unicodeAlpha alpha, alphaNumeric and alphaDash accept Unicode letters, like José. shortInMessage The default in message is The selected {field} is invalid, with no list of allowed values. dtoAllErrors A DTO runs the rules of every field with the right type, even when another field is missing or wrong. So one request gets all its errors at once. dtoRejectEmptyList A required List field of a DTO fails required on []. dtoMaybeRejectsEmpty A Maybe<T> field of a DTO fails required when the key is sent with an empty value, like "". laravelMessageKeys A custom message key can also use the short rule name, like name.min for the min_length error. See the list of names.

The three dto... flags need DTO code made by a current dox_builder, so run dart run build_runner build once after you turn them on.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
You can use dox_validation in any Dart program. Add the package, and the builder for DTOs:

dart pub add dox_validation
dart pub add dev:dox_builder dev:build_runner

import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

Run the DTO generator with dart run build_runner build.

docs.title: Database rules
docs.text:
exists and unique ask a PresenceVerifier. In a Dox app, dox_orm sets one when the database starts, so they just work. (@Unique and @Exists for DTOs are in dox_orm.)

Without Dox, or with another database layer, write your own. Each isolate has its own value, so set it in code that runs in every isolate:

class MyVerifier extends PresenceVerifier {
  @override
  Future<Set<String>> found(
    String table,
    String column,
    List<Object?> values, {
    String? exceptColumn,
    Object? exceptValue,
    String? connection,
  }) async {
    // Return the values that are in the column, as text.
    // Bind the values as query parameters, never put them into the SQL.
    return <String>{};
  }
}

class VerifierProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    PresenceVerifier.instance = MyVerifier();
  }
}

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
• Every schema and every DtoSchema implements the Standard Schema interface (StandardSchema). Code that only needs to validate can take any StandardSchema.
  • parse, safeParse, parseAsync and safeParseAsync also work on a DtoSchema, with Source.body. parse throws a StateError when the DTO has async rules.
  • In the JSON Schema, a nested DTO goes in $defs with a $ref, and @Dto(strict: true) adds "additionalProperties": false.
  • An app with no DTO gets an empty final list in dtos.g.dart.
  • Table and column names for exists and unique may use letters, digits, _ and $, with . between parts. Other names throw an ArgumentError when the schema is built.
  • unique never takes the column from the input key, because a key in v.map() comes from the user.
  • The database decides if two values match. On MySQL, TAKEN@dox.dev is taken when taken@dox.dev is there.
  • prohibited() fails on any sent value except blank text, also on null, [], 0 and false. prohibitedIf() lets null, blank text and empty lists or maps pass.
  • accepted() on v.string() or v.any() takes the exact words true, 1, "1", "true", "yes" and "on" (case sensitive). declined() takes false, 0, "0", "false", "no" and "off".
  • gtField, gteField, ltField and lteField fail when the other key is missing.
  • .bail() counts for all rules of that schema, wherever it is in the chain. On v.object() or v.list(), each field and item keeps its own setting.
  • excludeIf does not skip when the other key is missing. excludeUnless treats a missing key as null, so it skips. Both work only on a field of v.object(), not on a top-level value, list item or v.map() value. Other rules that read the skipped key still see its raw input.
  • A per-call MessageResolver falls back to the built-in text, not the global text.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
These are short pages to look things up: config fields, commands, env vars, errors and more.

Page What is on it App config every field of AppConfig and the config classes it holds, with type, default and meaning CLI every dox command, its options and the files it writes Environment variables every env var the framework and its packages read HTTP exceptions the exception classes, their status codes and the body a client gets Request and response the members of DoxRequest, DoxResponse and response() Troubleshooting known problems, the exact error text, the cause and the fix Cheat sheet one page of the code you use every day, with links to the full pages Production checklist what to check before you deploy, and what Dox does not do for you Error index every message Dox prints or throws, when it happens and what to do Changelog what changed in each package, newest first

docs.title: App config
docs.text:
This page lists every field of AppConfig, with its type, its default and what it does.

AppConfig is the one object you give to Dox().initialize(). It lives in lib/config/app.dart. Every field has a default except appKey, so you only set what you want to change. A full example is at the end of the page.

docs.title: Server
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning appKey String required Encrypts cookies and signs local storage URLs. It must be exactly 32 characters. Make one with dox key:generate. In production a bad key stops the app at start, see APP_ENV. serverPort int 3000 The port to listen on. When the env has no APP_PORT but has PORT, Dox uses PORT (Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it). host String? null: APP_HOST, else all interfaces The network interface to listen on, like 127.0.0.1. null reads APP_HOST. With neither, Dox listens on all interfaces (::). totalIsolate int? Platform.numberOfProcessors How many isolates (threads) serve HTTP, all on the same port. Windows always uses one. compress bool false gzip the responses.
