It costs CPU on every response, so let a proxy do it when you have one. maxBodySize int 10 * 1024 * 1024 (10 MB) Biggest JSON or urlencoded body in bytes. Bigger gets 413. maxMultipartSize int 100 * 1024 * 1024 (100 MB) Biggest multipart/form-data body (file uploads) in bytes. Bigger gets 413. bodyTimeout Duration Duration(seconds: 120) A client that sends no body bytes for this long gets 408. A slow but steady upload is fine. idleTimeout Duration Duration(seconds: 30) A keep-alive connection with no new request for this long is closed. Behind a load balancer, set it longer than the balancer's idle timeout. See Behind a load balancer. maxConnections int? null (no limit) The most connections one isolate holds open at once (1 or more). When it is full, new clients wait in the OS queue until a connection closes. The whole app holds up to maxConnections * totalIsolate, so keep that below ulimit -n. shutdownTimeout Duration Duration(seconds: 8) On SIGTERM or SIGINT, how long open requests may run before Dox closes them. Keep it below the kill timeout of your platform. See Graceful shutdown. trustedProxies List<String> [] IPs or CIDR ranges of your reverse proxies. Dox reads X-Forwarded-For (for req.ip()) and X-Forwarded-Proto (for req.scheme()) only from these. ['*'] trusts any direct client.

docs.title: Routing and request handling
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning container void Function(IocContainer)? null Pass registerContainer from lib/generated/container.g.dart. It fills the container, and also gives the routers, providers and model binders. See Dependency injection. routers List<Router> [] Routers to register first, in this order. Every other Router class comes from container. globalMiddleware List<dynamic> [] Middleware that runs on every route. A function or an IDoxMiddleware. dtos List<DtoSchema<Object>> [] Pass dtos from lib/generated/dtos.g.dart. Dox finds the DTOs of controllers and req.validate<T>() in it. validationMessages MessageResolver? null (English messages) Messages for validation errors, for example in other languages. responseHandler ResponseHandlerInterface? null A class with DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res). It sees every response before it is sent. exceptionHandler ExceptionHandler ExceptionHandler() Reports every unhandled error and turns it into a response. The default logs the error and the stack. See Error handling. htmlErrors bool false Sends an HTML error page to a request that does not want JSON. In development or local the page also shows the error and the stack. JSON clients do not change. See An HTML error page. errorPage String Function(int status, Object error, StackTrace stack, bool debug) defaultErrorPage Makes the HTML of the page. debug is true in development or local. Escape every value you put in the page. Used only with htmlErrors. providers List<DoxProvider> [] Providers to run first, in this order. Every other DoxProvider class comes from container. Dox runs them in every isolate at start. webSocketAllowedOrigins List<String>? null (no check) Checks the Origin of every Route.websocket route. Only the same host and the listed sites, like https://app.example.com, can open a socket. Others get 403. [] means the same host only. With null, any website can open a socket with the user's cookies, and Dox prints a warning at start.

docs.title: Sub configs
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning cors CORSConfig CORSConfig() CORS headers. See CORSConfig. logger LoggerConfig LoggerConfig() The Logger output. See LoggerConfig. cache CacheConfig file store in storage/cache, plus a memory store Cache stores for Cache(). See CacheConfig. session SessionConfig cookie driver, cookie dox_session, 2 hours Settings for SessionMiddleware. See Session. openApi OpenApiConfig OpenApiConfig() /docs, /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml. See OpenApiConfig. flags CoreFlags CoreFlags() (all off) Opt-in core behaviors. See Core flags.

docs.title: Core flags
docs.text:
CoreFlags turns on extra behaviors. Every flag is off by default, so you turn on only the ones you want:

AppConfig(
  appKey: env.appKey,
  flags: const CoreFlags(onlyPresent: true, cookieDefaults: true),
);

CoreFlags.all() turns on every flag:

AppConfig(appKey: env.appKey, flags: const CoreFlags.all());
Flag When it is on laravelErrors A 422 body is {"message": "...", "errors": {"field": ["..."]}}, with all messages of each field. The OpenAPI docs use this shape too. Off: {"field": "first message"}. onlyPresent req.only([...]) leaves out keys that are not in the input. So model.update(req.only([...])) does not write null for a field the client did not send. Off: a missing key is in the map with null. cookieDefaults A DoxCookie with no path gets Path=/, and one with no sameSite gets SameSite=Lax. A value you set wins. Off: no Path and no SameSite. hasKeyOnly req.has('x') is true when the key is there, with any value (also '' or null), like req.exists('x'). Dot keys work. Off: '' and null give false. htmlStrings A string from a controller is sent as text/html. A content type you set wins. Escape user input in the string. Off: text/plain. replaceHeaders res.header(k, v) replaces a value that a middleware set before. Vary and Set-Cookie still get one more value. Off: it adds a second value. Pass replace: to pick for one call. decryptServerError A DecryptException gives a 500 server_error, and the ExceptionHandler reports it. Off: 400 decrypt_failed, not reported. envExpand .env values can use ${OTHER}, and a "..." value reads \n, \t, \", \\ and \$. Also set Env.flags = flags; at the top of main() in bin/server.dart and in your tests, because .env is read before AppConfig exists. See Use one value in another. Off: values are read as written. rateLimitIpv6Prefix The default key of RateLimit counts an IPv6 client by its /64 prefix. One home or server gets a whole /64, so with one count per address a client gets a new count with each new address. Clients in one /64 share a count. A key you give is used as it is. Off: each full ip has its own count. See Rate limiting. cacheCopies Cache().store('x'), .tag() and .tags() give a new Cache, and the first one does not change. Off: they change the same object and give it back.

The cache has its own flag class, CacheFlags, in CacheConfig.

docs.title: CORSConfig
docs.text:
A value can be a String ('*' or a comma list) or a List<String>. A null value sends no header. Because every value is null by default, you must set at least origin.

Field Type Default Header enabled bool true Send CORS headers. A route can override it with its own cors setting. origin dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Origin. One origin, '*', or a list. With a list, Dox sends back only the request origin if it is in the list. methods dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Methods headers dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Headers exposeHeaders dynamic null Access-Control-Expose-Headers credentials bool? null Access-Control-Allow-Credentials maxAge num? null Access-Control-Max-Age in seconds

docs.title: LoggerConfig
docs.text:
Field Type Default Meaning name String '' Written as logger.name in each JSON log line. Left out when empty. enabled bool false Turn the Logger on. When it is off, LogMiddleware logs nothing too. prettyPrint bool false true prints colored text. Each line starts with a tag that says where it comes from, like [request], [server] or [app]. false prints one JSON object per line, for log services. The tag is then in the source field, unless your data already has a source key. level String 'info' The lowest level to print: debug, info, warn or error.

Your own lines get the tag [app]. To use another tag, pass it as the third argument. log, info, warn, success and danger all take it:

Logger.info('invoice sent', null, 'billing');

In JSON mode the tag is the source field. Plain warnings on stderr use the same tags.

docs.title: CacheConfig
StorageConfig
docs.text:
StorageProvider of the dox_storage package takes it. See File storage.

Field Type Default Meaning defaultDisk String 'local' The disk Storage() uses when no disk is named. disks Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>> {'local': {'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'}} Disk name to options. Each disk needs a driver option.

Options of each driver:

Driver Option Type Default Meaning all driver String required local, s3 or memory local root String storage Folder of the files. local url String none Base of the public URLs, like http://localhost:3000/files. local app_key String AppConfig.appKey Key that signs the URLs. local visibility String public public or private. local atomic_writes bool false Write to a temp file, then rename it. local permissions bool or Map off Visibility is the file mode. See File storage. s3 bucket String required Bucket name. s3 region String us-east-1 Region. s3 key String required Access key id. s3 secret String required Secret access key. s3 token String none Session token. s3 endpoint String none Custom endpoint (R2, MinIO, Spaces). s3 path_style bool false Use path style URLs. s3 url String none Base of the public URLs. s3 visibility String private public or private. s3 acl bool true The service supports ACLs. s3 batch_delete bool true The service supports batch delete.

docs.title: OpenApiConfig
docs.text:
Field Type Default Meaning enabled bool? null Serve the docs routes. null means on only in development or local. info Info Info(title: 'Dox API', version: '1.0.0') Title and version of the API. servers List<Server> [] Base URLs of the API. securitySchemes Map<String, SecurityScheme> {} Ways to log in, like {'bearerAuth': SecurityScheme.bearer()}. securityByMiddleware Map<String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>> {} Security for routes that use a middleware class with this name. It wins over @Security on the class. A middleware whose class name ends with AuthMiddleware gets bearerAuth when it has no @Security and no entry here. registry OpenApiRegistry OpenApiRegistry() (empty) What dox_builder found in the code. Pass openApiRegistry from lib/generated/openapi.g.dart. ui DocsUi DocsUi.scalar scalar or swagger. scalar ScalarOptions ScalarOptions() Options of the Scalar page. See below. pageTitle String? null (uses info.title) Title of the /docs page. include List<String> [] (all routes) Only routes with these paths are in the docs, like ['/api/*']. A * at the end matches the rest of the path. exclude List<String> [] Routes with these paths are left out. Checked after include.

ScalarOptions:

Field Type Default Meaning theme ScalarTheme ScalarTheme.default_ One of default_, alternate, moon, purple, solarized, bluePlanet, deepSpace, saturn, kepler, elysiajs, fastify, mars, laserwave, none. darkMode bool false Start in dark mode. showDownloadButton bool true Show the download button for the OpenAPI document. proxyUrl String? null Send "Try it" requests through this proxy.

docs.title: SocketIoConfig
docs.text:
SocketIoProvider of the dox_socketio package takes it. See Socket.IO.

Field Type Default Meaning enabled bool true Mount Socket.IO on the HTTP port at /socket.io/. options ServerOptions ServerOptions() Engine options. See below. namespaces List<NamespaceHandler> [] Namespaces to register, like ChatNamespace(). adapter SocketAdapterFactory? null (in memory with one isolate, IsolateAdapter with many) Makes the adapter in each isolate. Use a Redis adapter with many servers.

ServerOptions:

Field Type Default Meaning path String /socket.io/ URL path. Must end with /. pingInterval Duration 25 s Time between two server pings. pingTimeout Duration 20 s Time to wait for a pong before the session is closed. upgradeTimeout Duration 10 s Time a websocket upgrade may take. connectTimeout Duration 45 s Time a client has to join a namespace after the handshake. maxHttpBufferSize int 1000000 Biggest message in bytes a client may send. maxAttachments int 10 Most binary attachments in one packet. A packet with more closes that client. transports List<String> ['polling', 'websocket'] Allowed transports. allowUpgrades bool true Allow upgrades from polling to websocket. cors CorsOptions? null (no CORS headers) CORS for the long-polling requests.

CorsOptions:

Field Type Default Meaning origins List<String> ['*'] Allowed origins. credentials bool false Send Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. methods List<String> ['GET', 'POST'] Allowed methods for preflight. allowedHeaders List<String>? null (the requested headers) Allowed request headers. maxAge Duration? null How long a browser may cache the preflight answer.

docs.title: DatabaseConfig
docs.text:
The database is not a field of AppConfig. A provider calls SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig) in its setup().

Field Type Default Meaning connection String required Name of the connection to use. connections Map<String, ConnectionConfig> required Connection name to config.

ConnectionConfig:

Field Type Default Meaning driver Driver required Driver.postgres, Driver.mysql (also MariaDB) or Driver.sqlite. host String 'localhost' Database host. Not used by sqlite. port int 0 Database port. Not used by sqlite. user String '' Database user. Not used by sqlite. password String '' Database password. Not used by sqlite. database String required Database name. For sqlite: the file path, or :memory:. useSSL bool false Use TLS. Postgres: mode require (no certificate check), set extra['sslMode'] to change it. MySQL: the certificate is checked. debug bool required Print every query with printer. printer QueryPrinter? null ConsoleQueryPrinter(), PrettyQueryPrinter(), FileQueryPrinter(file: File('queries.log')) or your own. With buffered: true, call await printer.flush() before exit(), or the last lines are lost. logRedact List<String> [] Names of values to hide in the query log. A value shows as *** when its key ends with one of these names. ['password', 'token'] hides password, users.password and remember_token. Only the log changes. slowQueryMs int? null Log each query that takes longer than this many milliseconds. 0 logs every query. null turns it off. It works with debug off. read List<Map<String, dynamic>>? null Read replica hosts. Each map can change host, port, user, password, database and extra. See Read replicas. write Map<String, dynamic>? null Settings of the write host, in the same form as one read map. Only used with read. sticky bool false With read: after a write, the reads of the same request go to the write host. extra Map<String, dynamic> {} Driver options. See below. driverFactory DBDriver Function(ConnectionConfig)? null Your own driver class. It wins over every other setting.

Keys of extra:

Driver Key Type Default Meaning postgres, mysql maxConnectionCount int 10 Most open connections, for the whole process. postgres, mysql threads int 1 Rust threads of the native driver. Only the first pool sets it. postgres, mysql requestTimeout Duration 300 s The longest wait for one request (a free connection, the connect and the query). Over it, the request fails. postgres, mysql maxConnectionAge Duration none on Postgres, 12 hours on MySQL Close a connection older than this, once it has no query. postgres, mysql idleTimeout Duration no limit on Postgres, 12 hours on MySQL Close a free connection that is not used for this long. mysql serverKill bool true Stop a cancelled or timed out query on the server with KILL. Set false behind a proxy like ProxySQL. mysql, sqlite preparedStatementCacheSize int 100 Prepared statements kept per connection. postgres sslMode String require with useSSL, else disable TLS mode: disable, prefer, require or verify-full. postgres sslRootCert String none Path of a PEM file with the CA certificates to trust for verify-full. sslrootcert in DATABASE_URL. postgres sslWarning bool true false hides the warning Dox prints when TLS mode is require. sslWarning=false in DATABASE_URL works too. postgres timeZone String UTC Session time zone. postgres applicationName String none Name of the app in pg_stat_activity. mysql verifyCertificate bool true false skips the TLS certificate check. Only for a self-signed certificate in development. sqlite busyTimeout int 5000 PRAGMA busy_timeout in milliseconds. sqlite background bool false true runs the queries in a helper isolate, so a slow query does not block the request isolate. ?background=true in DATABASE_URL works too. See SQLite.

A time key takes a Duration, or a number of seconds. See Pool settings.

docs.title: AuthConfig
docs.text:
Auth is not a field of AppConfig. A provider calls Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(...)) in its setup().

Class Field Type Default Meaning AuthConfig defaultGuard String required The guard Auth() uses when no guard is named. AuthConfig guards Map<String, AuthGuard> {} Guard name to guard. AuthGuard driver AuthDriver required How a token is made and checked, like JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(...)). AuthGuard provider AuthProvider required Where users come from. AuthProvider model dynamic Function() required Makes the user model, like () => User(). AuthProvider identifierFields List<String> ['email'] Columns attempt() matches the login with. AuthProvider passwordField String 'password' Column with the bcrypt hash.

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
These are the config files of a new project. They read their values from env, the typed env class in lib/config/env.dart (see Env reference).

lib/config/app.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cache.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cors.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/logger.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';
import 'package:my_app/generated/container.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// Changing the key makes old cookies and encrypted data unreadable.
  appKey: env.appKey,
  serverPort: env.appPort,
  totalIsolate: env.appTotalIsolate ?? Platform.numberOfProcessors,
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    LogMiddleware(enabled: env.appEnv != 'production'),
  ],
  container: registerContainer,

  /// Only in development. Warns when a handler blocks the isolate.
  strict: StrictConfig(enabled: env.appEnv == 'development'),
  cache: cache,
  cors: cors,
  logger: logger,
);
lib/config/cache.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},

    /// one map per isolate, fast, not shared
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
  },
);
lib/config/logger.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

LoggerConfig logger = LoggerConfig(
  name: env.appName,
  enabled: true,
  level: env.logLevel,
  /// colored text is slow. JSON lines in production.
  // Env.appEnv, not appConfig.isDevelopment: appConfig is built from
  // this logger, so reading appConfig here would loop.
  prettyPrint: Env.appEnv == 'development',
);
lib/config/database.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// Print every SQL query only in development.
bool _debug = appConfig.isDevelopment;

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: env.dbConnection,

  /// Only in development. Warns about N+1 relation loads and big results.
  strict: OrmStrict(enabled: appConfig.isDevelopment),
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 5432,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{
        /// One pool for all isolates.
        'maxConnectionCount': 10,
        'maxConnectionAge': Duration(hours: 1),
      },
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// MySQL and MariaDB
    'mysql': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.mysql,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 3306,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{'collation': 'utf8mb4_general_ci'},
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// `DB_NAME` is a file path, or `:memory:`.
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: env.dbName,
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),
  },
);
lib/config/cors.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  enabled: false,
  // a list: Dox sends back the request origin only when it is in the list
  origin: <String>['http://localhost:3000'],
  methods: <String>['GET', 'HEAD', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'],
  headers: <String>[
    'accept',
    'authorization',
    'content-type',
    'x-csrf-token',
    'x-xsrf-token',
    'x-requested-with',
  ],
  exposeHeaders: <String>[
    'cache-control',
    'content-language',
    'content-type',
    'expires',
    'last-modified',
    'pragma',
  ],
  credentials: true,
  maxAge: 90,
);

Do not use origin: '*' together with credentials: true, because the browser refuses that pair and the call fails. '*' is fine for a public API without credentials.

lib/providers/orm_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/database.dart';

/// Dox finds it by itself and runs it in every isolate.
/// No database? Delete this file.
class ORMProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig);
  }

  @override
  Future<void> shutdown() async {
    await SqlQueryBuilder.close();
  }
}

A new project also has lib/config/storage.dart, queue.dart and schedule.dart, with a provider for each in lib/providers/. See File storage, Queue and Scheduler.

A new project has no openapi.dart, socketio.dart or auth provider. You add them when you need them. See OpenAPI, Socket.IO and Authentication.

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text:
This page shows the code you use every day, on one page you can keep open while you work.

Each section links to its full page.

docs.title: Project layout
docs.text:
Path What is in it bin/server.dart starts the app: Dox().initialize(), migrations, Dox().startServer() bin/migrate.dart runs migrations for dox migration:* bin/seed.dart runs seeders for dox db:seed bin/queue.dart the queue worker for dox queue:* bin/schedule.dart the scheduler for dox schedule:* bin/openapi.dart you add it: writes the OpenAPI files for dox openapi:generate lib/config/ app.dart (AppConfig), env.dart, database.dart, cors.dart, cache.dart, storage.dart, logger.dart, queue.dart, schedule.dart. You add others, like openapi.dart. lib/routes/ api.dart, web.dart: one Router class each lib/app/http/controllers/ <name>.controller.dart lib/app/dtos/<name>/ <name>.dto.dart lib/app/http/middleware/ <name>.middleware.dart lib/app/serializers/ <name>.serializer.dart lib/app/models/<name>/ <name>.model.dart lib/app/jobs/ <name>.job.dart lib/providers/ DoxProvider classes: ORM, storage, queue, schedule. You add others, like auth. lib/generated/ container.g.dart, openapi.g.dart, jobs.g.dart and dtos.g.dart (an empty list when the app has no DTO). Made by build_runner. Do not edit. db/migration/ migrations and migrations.dart (the registry) db/seeders/, db/factories/ seeders (seeders.dart is the registry) and model factories

See CLI and App config.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');
  }
}
Code Does Route.get('/blogs', (C c) => c.index) controller C from the container. Also post, put, patch, delete, options Route.get('/blogs', listBlogs) a plain function Route.post('/blogs', c.store, body: schema) body: is for the docs only. It checks nothing. Route.get('/blogs/{id}', c.show) path param. show(int id) Route.get('/posts/{page?}', c.list) optional param. list(int? page) Route.get('/docs/{path*}', c.page) rest of the path, with / Route.get('/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), c.me]) middleware first, controller last Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST'], '/contact', handler) one handler for a list of methods Route.any('/webhook', handler) one handler for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE Route.redirect('/home', '/') / Route.permanentRedirect('/old', '/new') send a path to another URL. 302 by default, 301 for permanentRedirect. Route.get('/users/{id}', c.show).where('id', '[0-9]+') the route matches only when the param fits the regex Route.fallback((DoxRequest req) { ... }) answers a GET or HEAD request that matches no route and no static file. Use it for a 404 page or an SPA. globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[const MethodOverride()] lets an HTML form reach PUT, PATCH and DELETE routes Route.group('/blogs', () { ... }) prefix. Dox adds the / between parts. Route.middleware(<dynamic>[M()], () { ... }) middleware for a group Route.domain('api.app.com', () { ... }) match by Host Route.resource('blogs', BlogController) index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy Route.health('/health') 200 {"status": "ok"}, or 503 when a check fails. See Health check. Route.staticFiles('/', 'public') serve a folder (CSS, JS, images) when no route matches. maxAge: sets Cache-Control Storage.route('files') serve a storage disk. Only signed URLs work, unless signed: false (dox_storage) Route.enabledCors(() { ... }) / Route.disabledCors(...) CORS for some routes Route.websocket('echo', (WebSocket s, DoxRequest req) { ... }) a raw WebSocket. For rooms and acks, use Socket.IO.

Controller parameters, by type: DoxRequest, one @Dto class, String/int/double/num/bool for path params (by position), a @DoxModel (loaded by its key), an @Inject() class. Only positional parameters.

In the examples, c.index and the like are methods of a controller C from the container.

docs.title: Dependency injection
docs.text:
@Inject()                       // one instance per isolate
class PostService {
  PostService(this.posts);      // from the container, by type
  final PostRepository posts;
}

@Inject(singleton: false)       // a new instance each time
class Clock {}

AppConfig(container: registerContainer); // from lib/generated/container.g.dart

Dox().ioc.get<PostService>();
Dox().ioc.override<PostRepository>(FakePostRepository()); // tests

Routers and DoxProvider classes are found without @Inject(). Run dart run build_runner build after a change. See Dependency injection.

See Routing and Controller.

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
class ApiKeyMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    String apiKey = Env.get<String>('API_KEY');
    // Hash.equals: constant time, so the time does not leak the key
    if (apiKey.isEmpty || !Hash.equals(req.header('X-Api-Key') ?? '', apiKey)) {
      return response('no').statusCode(401); // stop here
    }
    return req; // go on
  }
}
Middleware Does const RequestId() X-Request-Id header, req.requestId const ETag() ETag header, 304 when If-None-Match matches RequestTimeout(Duration(seconds: 30)) or Route.get(...).timeout(...) 503 when the route is too slow const ServerTiming() Server-Timing header; ServerTiming.add('db', d) adds a time. Development or trusted clients only const ValidateSignature() 403 unless the url is from Route.signedUrl(...) implements IDoxTerminableMiddleware terminate(req, res) runs after the answer is sent

Middleware runs in this order: globalMiddleware, router middleware, group, route.

See Middleware and Signed URLs.

Auth auth = req.auth as Auth; // after AuthMiddleware()

docs.title: Socket.IO
docs.text:
class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.join('lobby');
    socket.on('chat', onChat);
  }

  void onChat(SocketEvent event) {
    event.socket.to('lobby').emit('chat', event.data);
    event.ack('ok');
  }
}

Log users in at connect time with SocketAuth(findUser).handle in middleware. The user is in socket.user.

Turn it on with a SocketIoProvider (extend it in lib/). With many isolates, clients must use transports: ['websocket']. Broadcasts reach every isolate without Redis, but many servers need the Redis adapter.

See Socket.IO.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
This page lists every dox command, with its options and the files it writes.

To install the CLI, see the Dox CLI page. Run dox help to list the commands, and dox help <command> to see one.

A few rules hold for every command:

  • A name you pass becomes snake_case for the file and PascalCase for the class. So BlogPost and blog_post give the same result.
  • A make:* command never overwrites a file. When the file exists, it prints <name> already exists and stops.
  • Many make:* commands also answer to a create:* name, like create:model.
  • Packages and your app can add their own commands. See Package commands.

docs.title: dox create
docs.text:
dox create <project_name> [--version <version>]

Makes a new project from the dox-sample repo.

Option Meaning --version <v> (or --v) A release tag of dox-sample to clone. Without it, the newest dox-sample release with the same major version as the CLI is used.

It clones the template into a new snake_case folder, puts your project name in the files, and makes a .env with a new random APP_KEY. Then it prints the next steps: cd <name>, dart pub get and dox serve. It needs curl and git on the PATH.

The new project already has bin/server.dart, bin/migrate.dart, bin/seed.dart, bin/queue.dart and bin/schedule.dart, so the migration, seed, queue and schedule commands work in it right away.

docs.title: dox add
docs.text:
dox add <package> [--dev] [options]

Adds a Dox package and sets it up, like dox add orm --driver=postgres. orm is short for dox_orm.

It runs dart pub add and dart pub get. Then it runs the <package>:install command of the package, with your options, if the package has one. See Add a package.

docs.title: dox serve
docs.text:
dox serve [--no-reload] [--ignore-build-runner]
dox s
dox server

Starts the dev server with hot reload. It also runs dart run build_runner watch, so generated files stay up to date.

To change the port, set APP_PORT in .env, or run APP_PORT=9000 dox serve. A --port option is ignored.

Option Meaning --no-reload Turn hot reload off. Every change restarts the server. --ignore-build-runner Do not start dart run build_runner watch.

When you save a file, dox serve does one of these:

Changed Result A .dart file in lib/app/ (not .g.dart) Hot reload. The new code runs in the server at once, in about 0.1 to 0.2 seconds. Routes, providers, config, lib/generated/, bin/, db/ or a generated .g.dart file The server restarts, because this code or data is built only at start. A hot reload that fails, for example a compile error The server restarts.

Hot reload does not run code again that already ran. So a changed static or global value keeps its old value until a restart.

The server prints a VM service link at start. Open it in a browser to get DevTools (debugger, CPU profiler, memory). VS Code can also attach to it with "Dart: Attach to Dart Process".

docs.title: dox build
docs.text:
dox build

Compiles the app to a native binary for production, in build/bundle. Use this in production, not dart run.

It runs build_runner first (when the app uses it), then dart build cli. It also builds bin/queue.dart and bin/schedule.dart when they exist. Then run the app with cd build/bundle && ./bin/server.

It writes:

Path What build/bundle/bin/server the native binary, no Dart SDK needed build/bundle/bin/queue the queue worker, when bin/queue.dart exists build/bundle/bin/schedule the scheduler, when bin/schedule.dart exists build/bundle/lib/ native libraries from build hooks (SQLite, dox_http_native, ...) build/bundle/db/ your migrations and seeders. SQLite files are not copied. build/bundle/.env.example copy it to .env or set real env vars

Do not use dart compile exe. It can not build the native libraries.

docs.title: dox build_runner:build and dox build_runner:watch
docs.text:
dox build_runner:build
dox build_runner:watch

Run dart run build_runner build once, or dart run build_runner watch. build_runner:build prints a short output. Run dart run build_runner build yourself to see all of it.

docs.title: dox key:generate
docs.text:
dox key:generate [--show] [--force]

Makes a random 32 character key and writes it to APP_KEY in .env. Every other line of .env stays as it is. When there is no APP_KEY line, it adds one at the top.

Option Meaning --show Print a new key and write nothing. --force Skip the question below.

When APP_ENV=production, a new key logs every user out, so the command asks first. Without a terminal it prints a warning and runs. The .env file must exist.

docs.title: dox env:generate
docs.text:
dox env:generate

Writes lib/config/env.dart, the typed env class, from .env.example. It does not overwrite an existing file. Run dart run build_runner build after it.

The type of each getter comes from the example value:

Value in .env.example Getter a whole number, like 3000 int get x => 3000; true or false bool get x => true; empty String? get x; any other text String get x; (required)

A # comment line above a key becomes its doc comment.

docs.title: dox env:check
docs.text:
dox env:check

Checks the env with your AppEnv class, from the real environment and .env. It prints The env is valid., or every missing or bad key and exits with code 1. Run it in CI or before a deploy.

It needs lib/config/env.dart (see dox env:generate) and a name: in pubspec.yaml.

docs.title: dox openapi:generate
docs.text:
dox openapi:generate [dir]

Writes openapi.json and openapi.yaml into dir (default storage/openapi). It runs bin/openapi.dart, which a new project does not have. When it is missing, the command prints the code to put in it. See OpenAPI.

docs.title: dox update
docs.text:
dox update

Installs the newest CLI with the same major version as the one you have. It needs curl on the PATH.

docs.title: dox version
docs.text:
dox version
dox v
dox -v
dox --version

Prints the CLI version.

docs.title: dox help
docs.text:
dox help [command]
dox --help
dox -h

Without a command, it lists every command. With a command, it prints its usage, options and aliases.

docs.title: dox make:controller
docs.text:
dox make:controller <name> [-r|--resource] [--api] [--model=<model>]

Writes lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart. A trailing Controller in the name is removed, so UserController and User give the same file.

Option Meaning -r or --resource A resource controller with index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy. --api A resource controller without create and edit, the two form pages. Route.resource makes no route for them. --model=<model> or --model <model> A resource controller that uses the model. It imports package:<app>/app/models/<model>/<model>.model.dart. index returns all rows, and store creates a row from req.body. show, edit, update and destroy take the model as a parameter, so route model binding loads it by the {id}.

--api and --model work together, and each one makes a resource controller, also without -r.

The class has @Inject(), so the container makes it. A comment in the file shows the route to add. Run dart run build_runner build after it, so the controller is added to the container.

docs.title: dox make:middleware
docs.text:
dox make:middleware <name>

Writes lib/app/http/middleware/<name>.middleware.dart: a class <Name>Middleware implements IDoxMiddleware with a handle(IDoxRequest req) that returns req. A trailing Middleware in the name is removed.

docs.title: dox make:dto
docs.text:
dox make:dto <name>

Writes lib/app/dtos/<name>/<name>.dto.dart: a @Dto() class with one name field and part '<name>.dto.g.dart';. A trailing Dto in the name is removed: dox make:dto CreateBlog gives the class CreateBlog in lib/app/dtos/create_blog/create_blog.dto.dart. Run dox build_runner:build after it. See DTOs.

docs.title: dox make:serializer
docs.text:
dox make:serializer <name>

Writes lib/app/serializers/<name>.serializer.dart: a class <Name>Serializer extends Serializer<<Name>>. It imports the model with package:<app>/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart. A trailing Serializer in the name is removed.

docs.title: dox make:provider
docs.text:
dox make:provider <name>

Writes lib/providers/<name>_provider.dart: a class <Name>Provider extends DoxProvider with an empty setup() and an optional shutdown(). A trailing Provider in the name is removed: dox make:provider Cache gives CacheProvider in lib/providers/cache_provider.dart. Run dox build_runner:build after it, so Dox finds the provider. See Providers.

docs.title: dox make:command
docs.text:
dox make:command <name>

Writes lib/app/commands/<name>_command.dart: a class <Name>Command extends Command. Its name is app:<name>, and _ in the name becomes -. So dox make:command send_report makes the command app:send-report. A trailing Command in the name is removed.

It also adds the class to lib/app/commands/commands.dart, and adds dox: commands: to pubspec.yaml when it is not set. Then run dart pub get and dox app:send-report.

It makes all the changes or none. If a file is not in the shape it expects, it prints what to add by hand.

See Package commands.

docs.title: dox make:mail
docs.text:
dox make:mail <name> [--no-view]
Form Writes plain lib/app/mail/<name>_mail.dart and the view resources/views/emails/<name>.dox.html --no-view lib/app/mail/<name>_mail.dart only, with a plain text body

The class is <Name>Mail extends Mailable, and takes the recipient Address in its constructor. A trailing Mail in the name is removed. With the view, the mail uses the view emails/<name>. With --no-view, it has a text getter.

It tells you when pubspec.yaml still needs dox_mailer, or dox_view for the view.

See Mail.

docs.title: dox make:view
docs.text:
dox make:view <name>

Writes resources/views/<name>.dox.html with a small sample. A / in the name makes a folder, and each part becomes snake_case: Pages/About gives resources/views/pages/about.dox.html.

See Views.

docs.title: dox make:test
docs.text:
dox make:test <name> [--unit]
Form Writes plain test/<name>_test.dart that starts the app with DoxTestClient and checks GET /ping. Change the path to match your route. --unit test/<name>_test.dart with a plain package:test test. It does not start the app.

A trailing Test in the name is removed.

See Testing.

docs.title: dox make:model
docs.text:
dox make:model <name> [-m] [-c] [-r] [-f] [-s] [-a] [--api]
dox create:model <name> [-m] [-c] [-r] [-f] [-s] [-a] [--api]

Writes lib/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart, a @DoxModel class. The table name is the plural snake_case name, so BlogPost gives blog_posts. Add your columns to its empty fillable list.

Option Meaning -m or --migration Also make a create_<table>_table migration. -c or --controller Also make a plain controller, <name>.controller.dart. -r or --resource Also make a resource controller that uses the model. --api Also make a resource controller without create and edit, that uses the model. -f or --factory Also make a factory, db/factories/<name>.factory.dart. -s or --seed Also make a seeder, db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart. -a or --all Also make the migration, the factory, the seeder and a resource controller.

You can join short options: -mcr is the same as -m -c -r. With -c and -r together, the controller is a resource controller.

Each extra file is the same as the one from its own command:

Command Same file as dox make:model Post -m dox make:migration create_posts_table dox make:model Post -c dox make:controller Post dox make:model Post -r dox make:controller Post -r --model=Post dox make:model Post --api dox make:controller Post --api --model=Post dox make:model Post -f dox make:factory Post dox make:model Post -s dox make:seeder Post

When the model file exists, the command makes no file at all. When one of the extra files exists, only that file is skipped.

docs.title: dox make:migration
docs.text:
dox make:migration <name> [--sql]
dox create:migration <name> [--sql]
Option Meaning --sql Make a .sql file with -- up and -- down sections instead of a Dart class.

Writes db/migration/<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<hhmmss>_<name>.dart (or .sql). Migrations run in file name order, and a new file always sorts last.

For a Dart migration, it also updates db/migration/migrations.dart (the list of all migrations), and makes bin/migrate.dart when it is missing.

The code in the new file depends on the name:

Name up() down() create_<table>_table schema.create('<table>', ...) with id() and timestamps() schema.dropIfExists('<table>') <x>_to_<table>_table (also from, in, on) schema.table('<table>', ...) schema.table('<table>', ...) anything else a comment a comment

docs.title: dox route:list
docs.text:
dox route:list [--json]

Prints every route of the app: method, path, name, handler and middleware. Run it in the app folder.

METHOD  PATH           NAME  HANDLER             MIDDLEWARE
GET     /api/ping            ApiController.pong  LogMiddleware
GET     /ping                WebController.pong  LogMiddleware
GET     /docs                serve
GET     /openapi.json        serve
GET     /openapi.yaml        serve

5 routes
Option Meaning --json Print the same data as one JSON list. 
dox route:list --json

[{"method":"GET","path":"/api/ping","name":null,"handler":"ApiController.pong","middleware":["LogMiddleware"]}]

It does not start the server, and providers do not run. So a route that a provider adds, like the Socket.IO mount, is not in the list.

In the table, a function with no name shows as Closure. Fallback routes have the method FALLBACK, and Route.mount handlers have the method MOUNT.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
These commands run bin/migrate.dart of your app. If it is missing and you have Dart migrations, they make it first. With only .sql migrations, the CLI runs them itself.

The database comes from DATABASE_URL, or else from the DB_* keys. See Environment variables.

Command Aliases What it does dox migration:run dox migrate Run the migrations that did not run yet. dox migration:rollback [--step=<count>] [--batch=<number>] [--force] dox migrate:rollback Undo the last batch, the last <count> migrations, or only batch <number>. Give --step or --batch, not both. dox migration:reset dox migrate:reset Undo every migration. dox migration:refresh dox migrate:refresh Undo every migration, then run them all again. dox migration:fresh dox migrate:fresh Drop every table, then run all migrations. dox migration:status dox migrate:status Print which migrations ran, and their batch.

Add --seed to migration:run, migration:refresh or migration:fresh to run dox db:seed after the migrations.

When APP_ENV=production, the commands that undo or drop ask first. Add --force to skip the question.

docs.title: Factories and seeders
docs.text: Command Aliases What it does dox make:factory <model> dox create:factory Make db/factories/<model>.factory.dart. It imports the model with the package name of pubspec.yaml. dox make:seeder <name> dox create:seeder Make db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart. It updates db/seeders/seeders.dart, and makes bin/seed.dart when it is missing. dox db:seed [--class=<name>] Run the seeders with bin/seed.dart. The default seeder is DatabaseSeeder.

docs.title: Queue
docs.text:
These commands run bin/queue.dart of your app, which a new project already has. Ctrl+C and SIGTERM are passed on, so a worker can finish its job before it stops.

Command Runs What it does dox make:job <name> Make lib/app/jobs/<name>.job.dart with a @Job() class that extends DoxJob. It makes bin/queue.dart when it is missing. Run dox build_runner:build after it. dox queue:work [flags] bin/queue.dart work [flags] Run the worker. dox queue:failed bin/queue.dart failed List the failed jobs. dox queue:retry <id\|all> bin/queue.dart retry <id\|all> Put one failed job, or all of them, back on the queue. dox queue:forget <id> bin/queue.dart forget <id> Delete one failed job. dox queue:flush bin/queue.dart flush Delete all failed jobs. dox queue:clear [queue] bin/queue.dart clear [queue] Delete the jobs of a queue. The default queue is default. dox queue:restart bin/queue.dart restart Make the running workers stop after their current jobs. The workers must share the cache store. dox queue:prune-failed [--hours=N] bin/queue.dart prune-failed [--hours=N] Delete failed jobs older than N hours. The default is 24. dox queue:table From dox_queue_database. Make a migration for the queue tables. dox auth:tokens-table From dox_auth. Make a migration for the auth_access_tokens table.

Flags of queue:work:

Flag Default Meaning --queue=a,b default The queues to read, the first one first. --concurrency=N 1 How many jobs run at the same time in this process. --once off Run one job, then stop. --tries=N 1 How many times a job may run before it is marked as failed. A job can set its own tries. --timeout=S 60 Seconds a job may run. --sleep=S 3 Seconds to wait when the queues are empty. --stop-when-empty off Stop when the queues are empty. --timeout-grace=S none After a timeout, wait up to S seconds for the old run to end before the next try.

Flags of auth:tokens-table:

Flag Meaning --uuid The users have uuid ids. Set uuidIds: true on AccessTokenAuthDriver too. --string-ids The users have text ids. Set stringIds: true on AccessTokenAuthDriver too. Do not use it with --uuid. --users-table=<table> Add a foreign key from tokenable_id to this table, with cascade delete. --users-key=<column> The column of --users-table for the foreign key. Default: id. It does nothing without --users-table.

This is the bin/queue.dart of a new project. The jobs come from queueConfig in lib/config/queue.dart:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_queue/dox_queue.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await QueueWorker(app: appConfig).run(args);
}

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
These commands run bin/schedule.dart of your app, which a new project already has.

Command Runs What it does dox schedule:work bin/schedule.dart work Run the scheduler and keep it running. dox schedule:run bin/schedule.dart run Run the tasks that are due now, once. dox schedule:list bin/schedule.dart list List the scheduled tasks. dox schedule:test <name> bin/schedule.dart test <name> Run one task now. dox schedule:clear-cache bin/schedule.dart clear-cache Remove the withoutOverlapping() locks that a crash left behind. Do not run it while a task runs.

You add tasks in lib/config/schedule.dart. These are the two files of a new project:

lib/config/schedule.dart
import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';

ScheduleConfig scheduleConfig = const ScheduleConfig();

void schedule(Schedule s) {
  // s.call('cleanup', cleanup).dailyAt('02:00');
}
bin/schedule.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/schedule.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await SchedulerRunner(
    schedule: schedule,
    app: appConfig,
    config: scheduleConfig,
  ).run(args);
}

See Scheduler for the task methods, and Queue for jobs.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
This page lists every env var that Dox and its packages read.

To read your own keys with the typed env class, see Environment Variables.

docs.title: Read by the framework
docs.text:
APP_ENV changes how strict Dox is, so set it first:

  • development or local: Dox shows error details in 500 answers and health checks, turns /docs on (when openApi.enabled is null), and turns the dox_view template cache off.
  • development, local, test or testing: a bad APP_KEY or a JWT secret under 32 bytes is only a warning.
  • Any other value, or no value: Dox treats the app as production. A bad key stops the app at start, /docs is off and error details are hidden.

So set APP_ENV=development in your local .env and in CI.

Variable Who reads it Default Meaning Example APP_ENV dox_core, dox_auth, dox_view empty See the list above. A bad APP_KEY is one that is missing, not exactly 32 characters, or a public sample key. testing as a real env var also loads .env.testing. APP_ENV=production APP_NAME dox_core (Cache) not set The default prefix of a redis cache store: My Shop gives my_shop_cache:. So two apps on one Redis do not share keys. APP_NAME="My Shop" APP_URL dox_core (Route.signedUrl) not set The scheme and host in front of an absolute signed URL. APP_URL=https://example.com PORT dox_core (DoxServer.portFor()) not set The port to listen on, when APP_PORT is not set. Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it. PORT=8080 APP_HOST dox_core (DoxServer.hostFor()) not set (all interfaces, ::) The host to listen on. 127.0.0.1 keeps the app off the network, for an app behind a proxy on the same machine. AppConfig.host wins over it. APP_HOST=127.0.0.1 DATABASE_URL dox_orm (DatabaseConfig.url), dox_migration not set A database url. It wins over DB_CONNECTION and the other DB_* keys. The app reads it with the line url: env.databaseUrl in lib/config/database.dart. Without that line, only the shell value is read. See Database url. DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:secret@db:5432/blog?sslmode=require DB_CONNECTION dox_migration (DbConnection.config()) sqlite sqlite, postgres or mysql. Any other value is an error. DB_CONNECTION=postgres DB_HOST dox_migration localhost Database host. A path that starts with / is a Unix socket: the folder for Postgres, the socket file for MySQL. DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PORT dox_migration 5432 (postgres), 3306 (mysql) Database port. DB_PORT=5432 DB_USERNAME dox_migration postgres (postgres), root (mysql) Database user. DB_USERNAME=app DB_PASSWORD dox_migration postgres (postgres), empty (mysql) Database password. DB_PASSWORD=secret DB_DATABASE dox_migration falls back to DB_NAME, then dox Database name. For sqlite: the file path. DB_DATABASE=dox DB_NAME dox_migration dox Same as DB_DATABASE. DB_DATABASE wins when both are set. DB_NAME=dox HOME / USERPROFILE build hooks of dox_http_native, dox_postgres_native, dox_mysql_native empty Used to find cargo when a native library must be built from source. set by the OS DART_VM_OPTIONS the Dart VM not set Flags for the Dart VM. The binary from dox build reads it. Dox never sets VM flags for you. See Performance. DART_VM_OPTIONS=--new_gen_semi_max_size=64

docs.title: Read by a new project
docs.text:
A new project (dox create) reads these keys with its typed env class in lib/config/env.dart. The framework itself does not read them. In code, use the getter, like env.appPort.

Variable Getter Type Default Used for APP_NAME appName String dox LoggerConfig.name. APP_ENV appEnv String production development, staging or production. development turns on colored logs and the query log. Any value except production turns on LogMiddleware (one log line per request). The framework reads it too, see above. APP_PORT appPort int 3000 AppConfig.serverPort. When it is not set, Dox uses PORT if the env has it. APP_KEY appKey String required AppConfig.appKey. Exactly 32 characters. Run dox key:generate to make one. APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE appTotalIsolate int? not set: one per CPU core AppConfig.totalIsolate. LOG_LEVEL logLevel String info LoggerConfig.level. CACHE_STORE cacheStore String file CacheConfig.defaultStore. A new project has the stores file and memory. Add a redis store in lib/config/cache.dart before you use it. STORAGE_DISK storageDisk String local StorageConfig.defaultDisk. A new project has the disk local. Add an s3 or memory disk in lib/config/storage.dart before you use it. DB_CONNECTION dbConnection String sqlite DatabaseConfig.connection: sqlite, postgres or mysql. DB_NAME dbName String db/dox.sqlite The database name. For SQLite: the file path. DB_HOST dbHost String localhost Database host. DB_PORT dbPort int? not set: 5432 for Postgres, 3306 for MySQL Database port. DB_USERNAME dbUsername String postgres Database user. DB_PASSWORD dbPassword String empty Database password.

To add a key, add a getter to AppEnv and run dart run build_runner build. See Environments.

The .env.example of a new project:

.env.example
APP_NAME=dox
APP_ENV=development
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=

CACHE_STORE=file
STORAGE_DISK=local

# SQLite needs no setup. The file is created at the first start.
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite

# Postgres or MySQL: set DB_CONNECTION=postgres or mysql and fill these in.
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=postgres

docs.title: How .env is parsed
docs.text:
A real environment variable always wins over the .env file. The file is read like this:

  • One KEY=value per line. A line that starts with # is a comment.
  • export KEY=value is read like KEY=value.
  • The value is everything after the first =, so DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@h/db?a=b works.
  • A # after a space starts a comment: KEY=abc # note gives abc. KEY=abc#def stays abc#def.
  • Quotes (", ' or `) keep the value as it is, also a #. The quotes are removed.
  • An empty value (KEY=), only spaces, or the text null counts as missing. So Env.get gives the default.
  • In tests (dart test, or APP_ENV=testing as a real env var), Dox also reads .env.testing. Its keys win over .env.
  • With CoreFlags.envExpand, ${OTHER} and "..." escapes work. See Use one value in another.

Migrations (dox_migration) use their own simpler parser. It does not strip # note comments, so keep comments on their own line.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
• Env.get() and EnvReader read the real environment and .env. Code that reads Platform.environment sees only the real environment.
  • The .env file is read once per isolate, from the current folder.
  • The parser of dox_migration removes every quote character, has no ${VAR} expansion, and does not read .env.testing.

docs.title: Error index
docs.text:
This page lists the messages Dox prints or throws, so you can search for the text you see.

A <...> part changes, like a name or a number. Dart puts a prefix in front of some errors, like Bad state: or Invalid argument(s):. For problems that need a longer fix, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: dox_core: start of the app
docs.text: Text When What to do APP_KEY is not set. Rundox key:generateand put the key in .env appKey is empty. The app stops. In development, local, test or testing it is only a warning. Run dox key:generate, or set APP_KEY in the env. APP_KEY must be exactly 32 characters. Rundox key:generate`` The key is shorter or longer. Same rule as above. Run dox key:generate. APP_KEY is a public sample key. Rundox key:generatefor a new one The key is a known sample key. Same rule as above. Run dox key:generate. Unsupported operation: dox_http_native did not load: <reason>. Fix: ... The native HTTP library is missing or from another version. The app stops at start. Do what the Fix: part says. See Troubleshooting. Server started at http://<host>:<port> with <n> isolate (native) Normal start. <host> is the address it listens on: [::] means all interfaces. Nothing. Windows: the native server runs on one isolate Windows has no SO_REUSEPORT. Nothing. Socket.IO runs on <n> isolates: clients should use transports: ['websocket'] ... Socket.IO with more than one isolate and long-polling on. Use transports: ['websocket'] in the client. [server] isolate <n> error: <error> An error killed a worker isolate. The stack is on the next line. Fix the error. Dox restarts the isolate. [server] isolate <n> exited, restarting A worker isolate died. A new one starts after 1 second. Look at the error line above it. SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>) (OS Error: errno = <errno>), port = <port> The port is in use. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: dox_core: routes and controllers
docs.text:
These stop the app at start, so a bad route never reaches a request.

Text When What to do Route <where>: the controller parameter type <T> is not known. Use DoxRequest, a @Dto class, an @Inject class, a @DoxModel, a type from Route.bind, or String, int, double, num, bool for path params. ... A controller parameter has another type, the DTO is not in AppConfig.dtos, the class is not in the container, or there is no Route.bind<T> for a {param} of the route. Change the type or add the binder. Run dart run build_runner build, and set dtos: dtos and container: registerContainer in AppConfig. Route <where>: the action gives a function. Give it one controller parameter from the container, like (UserController c) => c.index. ... A route action like (c) => c.index where Dox can not find the controller class. Give the parameter its type, and mark the controller class with @Inject(). Bad state: <T> is not in the container. Add @Inject() above the class and rundart run build_runner build. ... Dox needs a class that is not in the container. Do what the text says, and set AppConfig(container: registerContainer). Route name "<name>" is used twice: <method> <path> and <method> <path>. Two routes have the same name. Give one of them another name. Invalid argument (name): No route has this name: "<name>" route() or Route.url() with a name that no route has. Check the name and the group name: prefix. Invalid argument(s): Route "<name>" (<path>) needs the param "<param>". route() without a value for a {param}. Pass it in params:. Invalid argument(s): An absolute url needs a host. ... route() with absolute: true and no APP_URL and no baseUrl:. Set APP_URL, or pass baseUrl:. Bad state: No bound value of type <T> for the route param "<param>". ... req.bound<T>() for a param with no Route.bind, or of another type. Add Route.bind<T>('<param>', ...). Route <where>: the controller has more path params than the route has {...} params (<n>). The method asks for more path params than the path has. Add the {param} to the path, or remove the parameter. Route <where>: a controller can have one @Dto only. Two DTO parameters. Merge them into one DTO. Route <where>: only positional parameters are supported, not named or [optional] ones (<type>). Named or [optional] parameters. Use positional parameters. Use int? with {id?} for an optional param. Route <where>: a controller can not be generic. The handler has type parameters. Remove them. Route <where>: can not read the controller type <type>. Dox can not read the function type of the handler. Use a plain method or function.

docs.title: dox_core: env
docs.text:
Text When What to do EnvException: the env is not valid then - <KEY> is missing AppEnv.load() found a required key with no value. Set the key, or give the getter a default. - <KEY> must be <type> A value does not fit the getter type. Fix the value. Check for a # comment after it. Env key "<KEY>" is not set and has no default Env.get<int>(), <num>, <double> or <bool> with no value and no default. Set the key, or pass a default. Env key "<KEY>" is not a valid <type> Env.get<int>() (or another type) got text that is not that type. Fix the value.

See Environment variables.

docs.title: dox_core: requests (what the client gets)
docs.text:
An IHttpException with a text message answers {"code":"<errorCode>","message":"<text>"}. The table shows the message text.

Status Message When What to do 404 <METHOD> <path> not found No route matches. Check the method, the path and the router prefix. 404 Not Found A typed path param does not fit, like abc for int id, or a Route.bind finds no row. Send a valid value. 400 The body is not valid JSON A DTO reads a JSON body that does not parse. Send valid JSON. 400 The form body is not valid A urlencoded body that can not be decoded. Fix the client encoding. 415 Unsupported Media Type A DTO reads a body that is not JSON or form data. Send Content-Type: application/json or form data. 413 Payload Too Large The body is bigger than maxBodySize or maxMultipartSize. Send less, or raise the limit. 419 CSRF token mismatch CsrfMiddleware finds no CSRF token, or a wrong one, on a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. Send the token. See CSRF. 429 Too Many Requests A RateLimit middleware sees too many requests. The Retry-After header says how many seconds to wait. Wait, then try again. See Rate limiting. 422 {"_root":"The input has too many items (max 1000) or levels (max 10)"} Form or query keys with more than 1000 list items or 10 levels. Send less nested data. 422 {"<field>":"<message>"} A DTO check failed. The core flag laravelErrors changes the shape. See Validation rules. 431 (no text) Native server: request line plus headers over 16 KB. Send smaller headers or cookies. 500 Server Error, code server_error. In development or local, the body is the error text. Any error that is not an HTTP exception. It also goes to ExceptionHandler.report. Look at the server log.

docs.title: dox_core: DTOs, storage and config
docs.text: Text When What to do Bad state: This request has no session. Add SessionMiddleware() to globalMiddleware or to the route. req.session on a route with no SessionMiddleware. Do what the text says. See Session. Bad state: <T> is not a known DTO. Add @Dto() to it, rundart run build_runner buildand setdtos: dtos(lib/generated/dtos.g.dart) in AppConfig. req.validate<T>() can not find T. Do what the text says. Invalid argument(s): Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>" A disk in StorageConfig has a driver other than local, s3 or memory. Fix the driver name. Invalid argument(s): Storage disk "<name>" needs the "<setting>" setting. It is missing or empty. An s3 disk without bucket, key or secret, on its first use. Set AWS_BUCKET, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Invalid argument(s): invalid file Storage().putFile() with bytes and no extension:, and Dox can not find the type from the bytes. Pass extension: 'pdf'. 403 invalid or expired signature A Storage.route() URL without a valid signature, or after expires. Make a new link with Storage().signedUrl(). 404 file not found Storage().stream(), download(), copy(), move(), getVisibility(), setVisibility(), size() or lastModified() of a missing file. Check the path. Invalid argument (trustedProxies): not an ip or cidr: "<value>" A bad entry in AppConfig.trustedProxies. Use an IP, a CIDR like 10.0.0.0/8, or *. Invalid argument (type): must be asc or desc: "<value>" orderBy(column, type) with another direction. Use asc or desc. 400 decrypt_failed, The encrypted value is not valid AESEncryptor.decode got changed text or a wrong key. req.cookie() gives null instead. The core flag decryptServerError makes it a reported 500. Check the key. For a cookie, ask the user to log in again.

docs.title: dox_auth
docs.text:
Text When What to do 401 Authentication failed AuthMiddleware finds no token, a bad or expired token, or the user is deleted. Send Authorization: Bearer <token>. Log in again. Invalid argument(s) (password): The password is too long. bcrypt takes at most 72 bytes. Hash.make() or Hash.makeAsync() with a password over 72 bytes. Limit the length in the DTO. See Troubleshooting. Invalid argument(s) (secret): The JWT secret is empty. Set APP_KEY (rundox key:generate). JwtAuthDriver with an empty secret. Set APP_KEY. Invalid argument(s) (secret): The JWT secret is <n> bytes. It must be at least 32 bytes. ... A short secret. In development, local, test and testing it is only a warning. Run dox key:generate. 401 The access token was already rotated. rotateAccessToken on a token that was rotated before. A token can be rotated only once. Use the new token. Bad state: The table 'auth_access_tokens' has no rotated_at column. ... rotateAccessToken on a token table without the rotated_at column. Add the column in a migration. See Authentication.

Hash.verify() gives false for a value that is not a bcrypt hash. It does not throw. Auth().attempt() returns null for a wrong password. It does not throw. More auth errors are in Authentication: Problems.

docs.title: dox_orm
docs.text: Text When What to do Unsupported operation: dox_postgres_native did not load: <reason>. Dox needs it to talk to Postgres. Fix: ... The native Postgres library did not load. The app stops. Follow the fix in the message. See Postgres native. Unsupported operation: dox_mysql_native did not load: <reason>. Dox needs it to talk to MySQL. Fix: ... The native MySQL library did not load. The app stops. Follow the fix in the message. See MySQL native. PgServerException(<code>): <message> The Postgres server refused the query, for example code 23505 for a unique violation. Read code, detail and constraint on the exception. MysqlException(<code>, <sqlState>): <message> An error from MySQL, for example code 1062 for a duplicate key. Read code and sqlState on the exception. Exception: <name> not found DatabaseConfig.connection (or withConnection()) names a connection that is not in connections. Fix DB_CONNECTION or the map. For a connection error, check DATABASE_URL or the DB_* values. A real env var wins over .env. docs.title: dox_cache
docs.text:

Add the store to CacheConfig.stores, or fix CACHE_STORE. Invalid argument(s): Cache driver "<driver>" of store "<name>" is not supported A store has a driver other than file, memory, redis or null. docs.title: dox_storage
docs.text:
The text has the form <Exception>: <message> (key: "<key>").

Text When What to do FileNotFoundException: File not found The file is not on the disk. Check the path. Storage() paths start with /, Disk keys do not. PermissionDeniedException: Permission denied The OS (local) or S3 (403) refused it. Check file rights, or the S3 key and bucket policy. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: path traversal is not allowed A key with ... Do not build keys from user input. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: absolute paths are not allowed A Disk key that starts with / or a drive letter. Remove the first /. InvalidKeyException: Invalid key: key is empty An empty key. Storage().deleteDirectory() with '', '/' or '.' also gives it, because the root is refused. Pass a file or folder name. UnsupportedOperationException: urlBase and appKey are needed for signed URLs signedUrl() on a local disk with no url, or no APP_KEY. Set both. UnsupportedOperationException: S3 signed URLs must expire within 1 second and 7 days signedUrl() on S3 with a bad expiresIn. Use a time up to 7 days. UnsupportedOperationException: Disk "<name>" is not registered Storage().disk('<name>') with a missing disk. Add the disk to StorageConfig.disks. DriverException: <S3 error> Any other S3 error (network, 500, wrong bucket). Read the S3 code in the text.

Use parseAsync() instead. Same, for one AsyncRule. Same. Bad state: This refine is async. Use parseAsync() instead. refine() with an async function and sync parse. Same. These stop dart run build_runner build.

Text When What to do The @Dto class <Name> has problems: then a - ... list One or more lines below. Fix each line. - The field <Class.field> must be final. A DTO field is not final. Add final. - The field <Class.field> must be athis.parameter of the unnamed constructor. The field is not set by the constructor. Add this.<field> to the constructor. - A @Dto class needs an unnamed constructor. Only named constructors. Add const Name({...}). - A @Dto class can not extend another class (<Parent>). The DTO extends a class. Copy the fields in. - A @Dto class can not be generic. The DTO has type parameters. Remove them. - The type <T> of <where> is not supported. Use a basic type, an enum, DateTime, RequestFile, a @Dto class, or a List or Map of them. Field type not supported. Change the type. - @<Rule> does not fit the type <T> of <where>. A rule on the wrong type, like @Email() on an int. Move the rule, or change the type. - @Length on <where> needs min:, max: or both. @Length() with no limit. Add min: or max:. - The @Regex on <where> is not a valid regex: <reason> The pattern does not compile. Use '2MB'. - @Dimensions on <where> needs at least one limit, like minWidth:. @Dimensions() with no limit. Add it. - <where> can not have both @Lowercase and @Uppercase. Both on one field. Keep one. - The validate method of <Name> must take one DtoErrors:void validate(DtoErrors errors). docs.title: Native libraries (build hooks)
docs.text:
Printed during dart pub get, dox serve or dox build. <pkg> is dox_http_native, dox_postgres_native or dox_mysql_native.

When a library is missing, the app stops with the reason and the fix. dox_http_native stops at start. The database drivers stop when the ORM opens the database.

Text When What to do <pkg>: no native library for <os>-<arch>. No ready build for this OS and CPU. Install Rust. <pkg>: download <file>: <status> / <pkg>: download <file> failed: <error> The GitHub download failed. Check the network, then dart pub get again. <pkg>: sha256 of <file> does not match The downloaded file is not the expected one. Delete .dart_tool and try again. <pkg>: cargo build failed The build from source failed. Read the cargo output below it. Bad state: <pkg>: <path> does not exist The lib_path user define points to a missing file. Fix the path in pubspec.yaml. <pkg> did not load: the native library is not in the build (...). The app opens Postgres or MySQL, but pubspec.yaml skips that driver. Remove its skip line. See Skip unused drivers. Unsupported operation: dox_http_native can not detach the socket. Use NativeWebSocket.upgrade for a WebSocket. Code called detachSocket() on a response. Rust owns the socket. For a WebSocket use NativeWebSocket.upgrade(request).

docs.title: dox_socketio
docs.text:

The client gets 500. Check the client version and transport. dox_socketio: publish failed: <error> The Redis or isolate adapter could not publish. Redis adapter: check Redis. Isolate adapter: it should not happen, so report it as a bug. dox_socketio: bad adapter message: <error> The Redis or isolate adapter got a message it can not read. Check that every app on the channel runs the same version.
