docs.title: HTTP exceptions
docs.text:
An HTTP exception stops a request and sends an error answer with the right status code, like 404 or 403.

Every HTTP exception extends IHttpException. It has three fields: the status code, a short errorCode like not_found, and a message. You can throw it, or return it from a middleware or a controller.

docs.title: Throwing an exception
docs.text:
Throw one of the classes below when a request can not go on. For example, when a post does not exist:

throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');

The client gets a JSON body with the errorCode and the message:

HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
content-type: application/json

{"code":"not_found","message":"Blog not found"}

docs.title: The classes
docs.text:
Most classes take the named parameters message, errorCode and code. The table shows the defaults.

Class Package code errorCode Default message Dox throws it when BadRequestException dox_core 400 bad_request Bad Request the body can not be read, like JSON that is not valid UnAuthorizedException dox_auth 401 unauthorized Authentication failed AuthMiddleware finds no valid token ForbiddenHttpException dox_core 403 forbidden Forbidden never; it is for your own use NotFoundHttpException dox_core 404 not_found Not Found no route fits, a typed path param does not fit ({id} is not an int), or route model binding finds no row MethodNotAllowedHttpException dox_core 405 method_not_allowed Method Not Allowed the path has routes, but not for this method. The Allow header lists the methods. PayloadTooLargeException dox_core 413 payload_too_large Payload Too Large the body is bigger than maxBodySize or maxMultipartSize UnsupportedMediaTypeException dox_core 415 unsupported_media_type Unsupported Media Type a DTO reads a body that is not JSON and not form data TokenMismatchException dox_core 419 csrf_token_mismatch CSRF token mismatch CsrfMiddleware finds no CSRF token, or a wrong one ValidationException dox_core 422 validation_failed {} (a Map) a DTO or req.validate() finds bad input TooManyRequestsException dox_core 429 too_many_requests Too Many Requests a RateLimit middleware sees too many requests InternalErrorException dox_core 500 server_error Server Error never; it is for your own use QueryException dox_core 500 sql_query_error Error in sql query never; it is for your own use

docs.title: Any status: abort and HttpStatusException
docs.text:
Sometimes you need a status that has no class. Use abort(code). It stops the request and answers with that status:

if (post.userId != req.auth?.id()) abort(403);

You can also pass a message:

abort(404, 'No post with this id');

abort throws an HttpStatusException. Throw it yourself when you want to send headers too:

throw HttpStatusException(503, headers: {'retry-after': '60'});

Common codes get a default errorCode and message, like forbidden and Forbidden for 403:

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json

{"code":"forbidden","message":"Forbidden"}

Other codes get http_error and Error.

docs.title: What the client gets
docs.text:
The status is the code of the exception. The body is sent as JSON with Content-Type: application/json.

A text message gives {"code": "<errorCode>", "message": "<message>"}, as shown above.

If you want your own JSON shape for one error, pass a Map as the message. It is sent as it is, with no code key:

throw NotFoundHttpException(message: <String, String>{'error': 'not_found'});
// 404 {"error":"not_found"}

A ValidationException always has a map, with one entry per field:

HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
content-type: application/json

{"email":"The email is not a valid email","name":"The name is required"}

A form post with a session (SessionMiddleware) does not get this JSON. Dox flashes the errors and the old input to the session and redirects back. See Session.

docs.title: Other errors
docs.text:
Any other Exception or Error gives 500 with {"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}. When APP_ENV is development or local, the body is the error text instead, so you can see what went wrong.

These errors go to the report method of the exception handler. An HTTP exception with a 5xx code is reported too. One with a 4xx code is not.

docs.title: Making your own exception
docs.text:
If you need an error that Dox does not have, extend IHttpException and set the three fields in the constructor:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class PaymentRequiredException extends IHttpException {
  PaymentRequiredException({
    dynamic message = 'Please pay',
    String errorCode = 'payment_required',
    int code = HttpStatus.paymentRequired,
  }) {
    super.code = code;
    super.errorCode = errorCode;
    super.message = message;
  }
}

To give every error of your app the same JSON shape, override toResponse(). It returns the body.

More examples are on the Response page.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
• A path with no route answers 404 with the message <METHOD> <path> not found, like {"code":"not_found","message":"GET /nothing not found"}.
  • When the path has routes for other methods, the answer is 405 with an Allow header, like Allow: GET, POST, HEAD. Your responseHandler sees both, so you can change their shape.
  • A ValidationException from dox_validation (from schema.parse() in a controller) becomes the 422 ValidationException of dox_core, with the same errors.

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text:
This page lists what to check before you deploy a Dox app.

Go through each table once before your first deploy. Items marked Dox limit are things Dox does not do for you, so you must handle them outside Dox.

docs.title: Secrets and config
docs.text: Check How Read more APP_KEY is set, 32 characters and secret Run dox key:generate, or set a random value of exactly 32 characters in the real env. It signs JWT tokens and encrypts cookies. Never use the value from .env.example. Encryption APP_ENV=production Set it, or leave it empty: both mean production. Then a bad APP_KEY stops the app at start, /docs is off and error details are hidden. Use APP_ENV=development only on your machine and in CI. Env reference The env is complete Run dox env:check in CI or before the deploy. It exits with code 1 when a key is missing or bad. CLI No secrets in the image or in git Put .env in .dockerignore and .gitignore. Pass values as env vars (docker run -e, env_file:, systemd EnvironmentFile=). dox build copies only .env.example. Docker No comments after values in .env The app strips # note, but migrations keep it in the value. Put comments on their own line. Env reference

docs.title: Auth and passwords
docs.text: Check How Read more JWT tokens expire JwtAuthDriver.expiresIn is 1 hour by default. Pick a time that fits your app, like expiresIn: Duration(hours: 12). Authentication A JWT works until it expires The server keeps no token list by default. To revoke tokens, set revocation: true on JwtAuthDriver, or use AccessTokenAuthDriver (tokens live in a table). To log out everyone, change APP_KEY with no previousKeys. Authentication Passwords are hashed Use user.password = await Hash.makeAsync(input) (bcrypt). It runs in another isolate, so other requests do not wait. Never store or encrypt a plain password. Hashing The hash is never sent Add List<String> get hidden => <String>['password']; to the user model. The JWT payload is user.toJson(), and anyone can read it. Authentication Passwords have a max length bcrypt takes at most 72 bytes, and Hash.make throws on longer input. Add @MaxLength(72) to the password field of the DTO. Troubleshooting

docs.title: HTTP and network
docs.text: Check How Read more HTTPS at the proxy Dox has no TLS server. Run Caddy or nginx in front. Keep the app port private. Deployment trustedProxies is set behind a proxy Set AppConfig(trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1']), or the proxy network, like '172.16.0.0/12'. Without it, req.ip() is the proxy and req.scheme() is http. Do not use ['*'] when the app port is public. App config Body limits are on Keep maxBodySize (10 MB) and maxMultipartSize (100 MB), or lower them. Set the same limit in the proxy: client_max_body_size 100m; Request CORS has real origins Use CORSConfig(origin: 'https://my.app'), or a list like <String>['https://my.app', 'https://admin.my.app']. CORS No credentials: true with origin: '*' The browser refuses this pair. The new project's cors.dart has credentials: true and a localhost origin. When you turn CORS on, put your real origins in the list. CORS Rate limiting Add RateLimit(...) to login and other busy routes. Use a Redis cache store, so all servers share the counts. You can also limit at the proxy. Rate limiting Security headers Add const SecurityHeaders() to globalMiddleware. Security headers gzip at the proxy Keep compress: false. Turn on gzip in Caddy (encode gzip) or nginx (gzip on;). Performance OpenAPI docs They are off in production. Do not set enabled: true for a private API. OpenAPI

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text: Check How Read more AOT binary, not dart run Run dox build, then build/bundle/bin/server. Keep bin/ and lib/ together. Do not use dart compile exe. Deployment Native server loads The start line says (native). If the library does not load, the app stops and prints the fix. Native server Native database driver loads The database works. If the library does not load, the app stops and prints the fix. Postgres native Isolates = cores Keep the default totalIsolate (one per CPU core), or set APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE to the cores the container really gets. Use fewer when the database runs on the same machine. With SQLite, 1-2 isolates are enough. Isolate Shared state across isolates Use a redis cache, not memory. For Socket.IO, use transports: ['websocket'] on the client, and a Redis adapter with many servers. Isolate A supervisor restarts the process Use Docker restart: unless-stopped, or systemd Restart=always. Dox restarts a dead worker isolate, but not the main isolate. Deployment Writable temp folder Uploads over 1 MB go to a temp file. A FROM scratch image needs /tmp with mode 1777. Docker Uploads live on a volume or S3 The local disk writes to storage/. Mount it as a volume, or use the s3 disk. File storage

docs.title: Database
docs.text: Check How Read more Postgres or MySQL for a busy app SQLite has one connection per isolate, and a query blocks the isolate, so use it for small apps only. Give it an absolute file path. Database Migrations run once per deploy The new project runs migrations in bin/server.dart before startServer(). Or run dox migrate once in CI. With many machines, run migrations in one place only, so two machines do not migrate at the same time. Migration Migrations use the right database Migrations also read a .env file, so a key that is only in an old .env is still used. Do not ship a .env next to the binary, or give Migrator(config: ...) your own config. Migration Small MySQL migrations MySQL saves CREATE, ALTER and DROP at once, so a failed migration can leave half the changes. Make one table change per migration. Migration Pool size fits the database Set extra: {'maxConnectionCount': 10}. All isolates share one pool, so this is the total for the process. Keep it under the database max_connections. Database Query logging is off debug: true prints every query. The new project turns it on only in development. Database Backups Dox limit. Dox has no backup tool. Use pg_dump, mysqldump, managed snapshots, or sqlite3 app.db ".backup x.db". Test a restore.

docs.title: Logs and errors
docs.text: Check How Read more JSON logs Use LoggerConfig(enabled: true, prettyPrint: false). The new project does this outside development. App config Log level Set LOG_LEVEL=warn to print only warnings and errors. App config Access logs in one place LogMiddleware logs one line per request. The new project turns it off in production, because the proxy already logs requests. Log lines are written every 20 ms, so a hard kill can lose the last lines. Performance Errors go to your tracker Extend ExceptionHandler and set AppConfig.exceptionHandler. Every error that is not an HTTP exception goes to its report method. Error handling

docs.title: Health and shutdown
docs.text: Check How Read more Health route Add Route.health('/health', checks: ...) with a database check, so the load balancer knows when the app can not serve. Health check Graceful shutdown On SIGTERM or SIGINT, Dox stops taking connections and lets open requests finish. Set shutdownTimeout below the kill timeout of your platform. Close your own connections in the shutdown() of a provider. Deployment Zero downtime deploys Run two processes (or machines) behind the proxy. Restart one at a time. Deployment

docs.title: Rate limit at the proxy
docs.text:
You can also limit requests at the proxy, so bad clients never reach the app.

nginx:

# in http { }
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=10r/s;

# in server { location / { } }
limit_req zone=api burst=20 nodelay;
limit_req_status 429;

Caddy needs the caddy-ratelimit plugin (build Caddy with xcaddy build --with github.com/mholt/caddy-ratelimit):

example.com {
  rate_limit {
    zone api {
      key    {remote_host}
      events 100
      window 1m
    }
  }
  reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}

Note

The proxy must see the real client IP. When there is a load balancer in front of the proxy, set the real IP module of the proxy first.

docs.title: Request and response
docs.text:
A short list of what you can use on DoxRequest, DoxResponse and the response helpers.

Examples and explanations are on the Request and Response pages.

docs.title: DoxRequest
docs.text: A controller gets a DoxRequest. So does a middleware that uses next (IDoxNextMiddleware). A simple middleware (IDoxMiddleware) gets an IDoxRequest, which has fewer members. The last column shows which members it has.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest validate<T>({Source? source}) Future<T> The request checked with the DTO T. Bad input gives 422. Throws StateError when T is not in AppConfig.dtos. no validateSchema<O>(Schema<O> schema) Future<O> Query and body checked with a fluent dox_validation schema. no all() Map<String, dynamic> Query and body together. Body wins on the same key. yes only(List<String> keys) Map<String, dynamic> Only these keys from all(). A missing key gives null. yes input(String key, [dynamic defaultValue]) dynamic One value from all(). A dot key like user.name or items.0.id reads inside maps and lists. You get the default when the key is not there or is null. IDoxRequest has no default value. yes except(List<String> keys) Map<String, dynamic> All values from all(), without these keys. no has(String key) bool true when the key is there and its text is not empty. yes exists(String key) bool true when the key is there, with any value (also '' or null). no missing(String key) bool true when the key is not there. no filled(String key) bool true when the key is there and not empty. Dot keys work. no boolean(String key, [bool defaultValue = false]) bool true for true, 1, on and yes. no integer(String key, [int defaultValue = 0]) int The value as an int. The default is used when the key is not there or is not a number. no file(String key) RequestFile? The uploaded file, or null when the field is not a file. no hasFile(String key) bool true when the field holds a file or a list of files. no add(String key, dynamic value) void Adds a value to all() and body. yes merge(Map<String, dynamic> values) void Adds many values to all() and body. yes body Map<String, dynamic> The parsed body (JSON or form fields). Files are RequestFile. no query Map<String, dynamic> The query string. no param Map<String, dynamic> The route params, like {'id': '5'}. no pathParams Map<String, String> The route params as text. null values are left out. no bound<T>(String param) T The value that Route.bind made for this route param. Throws StateError when there is none. no requestBody RequestBody The body as it was read, for DTOs. no isJson() bool The content type is JSON. yes isFormData() bool The content type is form data (multipart/form-data or urlencoded). yes toJson() Map<String, dynamic> all() with files replaced by their file name. Lets jsonEncode(req) work. yes

docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest header(String key) String? One header. null when it is not there. yes headers Map<String, dynamic> Every header. Many values of one name are joined. yes httpHeaders HttpHeaders The dart:io headers object. no contentType ContentType? The parsed Content-Type. yes bearerToken() String? The token of Authorization: Bearer <token>, or null. no cookie(String key, {bool decrypt = true}) String? One cookie. Decrypted with appKey unless decrypt: false. yes ip() String The client IP, or unknown. From X-Forwarded-For only behind a trusted proxy. yes scheme() String http or https. From X-Forwarded-Proto only behind a trusted proxy. no isSecure() bool scheme() is https. no clientIp String? The client IP, or null. no userAgent() String The User-Agent header, or unknown. yes host() String The Host header, or unknown. yes origin() String? The Origin header. yes referer() String? The Referer header. yes locale String? The first language of Accept-Language, like th. null when there is none or it is *. no auth IAuth? The auth object set by AuthMiddleware. req.auth?.id() gives the user id. It is null for a guest. yes expectsJson() bool The client wants JSON: an Accept header with json, a JSON body, or X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest. An Inertia request is not. no

docs.title: Session
docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest session Session The session of the request. Needs SessionMiddleware. Throws StateError without it. no hasSession bool true when the request has a session. no

docs.text: Member Returns What it gives On IDoxRequest method String The HTTP method in upper case. yes uri Uri The request URI. yes route RouteData The matched route. no getRouteData() RouteData Same as route. yes path() String The request path, like /admin/users/5. no fullUrl() String The full URL with the query string. no pathIs(String pattern) bool true when the path matches. * matches any text. no routeIs(String pattern) bool true when the route name matches. It is false for a route with no name. no getRouteIdentifier() String A key for the route (base64 of <method>|<domain><path>). Useful for a cache or rate limit key. yes httpRequest HttpRequest The dart:io request. Use it for raw access. yes

docs.title: DoxResponse
docs.text:
Every setter returns the same DoxResponse, so you can chain the calls.

Member Returns What it does DoxResponse(dynamic content) DoxResponse The constructor. content can be a String, number, Map, List, a JSON serializable object, a Stream<List<int>>, a File, a StreamFile or a DownloadableFile. statusCode(int code) DoxResponse Sets the status. Default 200. status int? The status set with statusCode(), or null (which means 200). content(dynamic content) DoxResponse Replaces the content. getContent() dynamic The content as it was given. stream(Stream<List<int>> stream) DoxResponse Sets a byte stream as content. contentType(ContentType type) DoxResponse Sets Content-Type. A File without it gets the type from its extension. header(String key, dynamic value) DoxResponse Sets one header. A second call with the same key replaces the value. cache-control and Cache-Control are one header. headers Map<String, dynamic> The headers set so far, by name. withHeaders(Map<String, dynamic> values) DoxResponse Adds these headers. A key replaces the header with the same name, in any case. Other headers stay. cookie(DoxCookie cookie, {bool setExpire = false}) DoxResponse Adds a Set-Cookie header. setExpire: true sends the cookie as expired, which removes it. cache(Duration duration) DoxResponse Sets Cache-Control: max-age=<seconds>.

docs.title: Response helpers
docs.text:
These top level functions give a DoxResponse.

Function What it does response([dynamic content]) Same as DoxResponse(content). redirect(String url, {int status = 302}) A redirect to url. It sets the Location header. back(DoxRequest req, {String fallback = '/'}) A 302 redirect to the Referer header, or to fallback when there is none.

docs.title: How the content is sent
docs.text:
A controller can return a plain value or a DoxResponse. Dox sends the content like this:

Content Sent as null an empty body String text, as it is Map, List, number, bool, object with toJson() JSON, Content-Type: application/json DateTime its ISO 8601 text File streamed, with Content-Length, Accept-Ranges and one Range supported StreamFile streamed with its content type. An HTML, XML or JavaScript type is sent as a download, in a sandbox. DownloadableFile streamed with Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<name>" Stream<List<int>> streamed chunk by chunk IHttpException its status and toResponse(), see HTTP exceptions other Exception or Error 500 with {"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}. In development or local, the body is the error text.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
This page lists known problems, with the text you see, the cause and the fix.

For short errors, search the Error index.

docs.title: The native HTTP library did not load
docs.text:
Symptom. The app stops at start with this error:

Unsupported operation: dox_http_native did not load: <reason>.
Fix: install Rust (cargo, see https://rustup.rs), then run the app again ...

At build time (dart pub get, dox serve or dox build) you may also see one of these:

dox_http_native: no native library for <os>-<arch>. Install Rust (cargo) to build it from source.
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext>: 404
dox_http_native: download dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> failed: <error>
dox_http_native: sha256 of dox_http_native-<os>-<arch>.<ext> does not match
dox_http_native: cargo build failed

Cause. The package could not find, download or build its native library. Common reasons:

  • There was no internet during dart pub get, or there is no ready build for your OS and CPU. Ready builds exist for macOS arm64 and x64, Linux x64 and arm64, and Windows x64.
  • Rust is not installed, so the library can not be built from source.
  • You compiled with dart compile exe. It does not run build hooks, so the binary has no native library.
  • The <reason> is native library ABI <x>, expected <y>. This means the library on disk is from another version of the package.

Fix. Pick one:

  1. Install Rust with rustup and run dart pub get again. Dox then builds the library with cargo.
  2. If the reason is an ABI mismatch and you set lib_path, rebuild that library: run cargo build --release in the native folder of the dox-http-native repo.

  3. Download the library yourself from the GitHub releases, and point to it in the root pubspec.yaml:

    hooks:
  user_defines:
    dox_http_native:
      lib_path: /path/to/libdox_http_native.so

  4. Build with dox build, not with dart compile exe.

The native database drivers load their library the same way. When it does not load, the app stops with:

dox_postgres_native did not load: <reason>.
dox_mysql_native did not load: <reason>.

The fix is the same as above, with the dox-postgres-native or dox-mysql-native repo.

See Native server, Postgres native and MySQL native.

docs.title: Port already in use
docs.text:
Symptom. At start:

SocketException: dox_http_native: bind failed (<code>) (OS Error: errno = <errno>), port = 3000

The errno is 48 on macOS and 98 on Linux.

Cause. Another process listens on the port. Often it is an old bin/server.dart that dox serve did not stop, or a second copy of the app.

Fix. Find and stop the process, or use another port.

lsof -i :3000          # macOS and Linux: who has the port
kill <pid>

Or set APP_PORT=3001 in .env (a new project reads it into serverPort).

docs.title: build_runner: conflicting outputs
docs.text:
Symptom. dox build_runner:build, dox serve or dox build stops with a build_runner message that starts with Conflicting outputs were detected, and names files like lib/generated/dtos.g.dart or lib/app/models/user/user.model.g.dart.

Cause. The generated .g.dart files are on disk, but .dart_tool/build does not know them. This happens after a git clone with committed .g.dart files, after deleting .dart_tool, or after a Dart SDK update.

Fix. Delete the build cache and build again:

rm -rf .dart_tool/build
dart run build_runner build

If that is not enough, delete the .g.dart files that the message names, and build again.

docs.title: Ambiguous import: Uuid, Name or Schema
docs.text:
Symptom. The analyzer or the build says a name like Uuid, Name, Range, Image or Schema is an "ambiguous import".

Cause. dox_core exports the validation rules (Uuid, Name, Range, Image, ...) and the Schema class. Another import has a class with the same name, like package:uuid. dox_orm also has a Schema class.

Fix. Hide the name you do not use in that file:

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' hide Uuid;
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

docs.title: A .env value with #
docs.text:
A # after a space starts a comment. The comment is not part of the value.

APP_PORT=3000 # dev port   -> 3000
DB_PASSWORD=abc#123        -> abc#123 (no space before the #)
DB_PASSWORD="abc # 123"    -> abc # 123 (quotes keep the #)

When a value must have # in it (a space, then #), put the value in quotes. The quotes are removed.

docs.title: Hash.make throws on a long password
docs.text:
Symptom. Saving a user, or registering, gives a 500. The log shows:

Invalid argument(s) (password): The password is too long. bcrypt takes at most 72 bytes.

Cause. Hash.make() and Hash.makeAsync() use bcrypt. bcrypt takes at most 72 bytes, so Dox throws an ArgumentError for a longer password. The error text does not hold the password.

Fix. Refuse long passwords in your DTO, before you hash them:

@MaxLength(72)
final String password;

@MaxLength counts characters, not bytes, so a password with non-ASCII characters can still be over 72 bytes. See Hashing.

docs.title: MySQL 8 login fails
docs.text:
Symptom. The connection to MySQL 8 is refused at login, while the same user works from the mysql client. Often the user was made with the default caching_sha2_password plugin.

Cause. caching_sha2_password needs either TLS or the server RSA public key to send the password. A client that has neither can not log in.

Fix. The Dox MySQL driver supports caching_sha2_password. Check these settings on the connection in lib/config/database.dart:

Setting What to do Remote host without TLS Turn on useSSL: true. useSSL: true The server must have TLS on. host, port, user, password A wrong value gives the same login error. DB_PORT is 3306 by default for MySQL.

As a last resort, change the user on the server:

ALTER USER 'app'@'%' IDENTIFIED WITH mysql_native_password BY 'secret';

docs.title: SQLite: the database file
docs.text:
Symptom. An SqliteException with unable to open database file, or an empty database after dox build.

Cause. A relative path is relative to the folder you start the app from. After dox build you run the app from build/bundle, so the default DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite becomes build/bundle/db/dox.sqlite. dox build does not copy your SQLite files, so that database starts empty. Also, SQLite makes a missing file, but not a missing folder.

Fix.

  • Use an absolute path, or make the folder first.
  • Set it with DB_NAME (a new project reads it): DB_NAME=/var/lib/my_app/dox.sqlite.
  • Migrations read DB_DATABASE or DB_NAME as the path too, so use the same value.
  • Do not use :memory: with more than one isolate. Each isolate gets its own empty database.

docs.title: dox: command not found after dart pub global activate
docs.text:
Symptom.

zsh: command not found: dox

right after dart pub global activate dox.

Cause. dart pub global activate puts the dox script in $HOME/.pub-cache/bin. That folder is not in your PATH.

Fix. Add it to your shell profile and open a new terminal:

export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"

On Windows the folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Pub\Cache\bin.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
dox_auth lets users register, log in and log out, and it protects routes so only logged in users can use them.

It gives you a password login against your user table, three ways to keep a user logged in (access tokens, JWT and sessions), AuthMiddleware to protect routes, and req.auth to get the user in your controller.

dox_auth has no password reset, no email check, no "remember me" and no two-step login (2FA). Your app builds these, and the tools on this page help, for example the two-step login recipe. Rules about who may do what are on the Authorization page.

docs.title: Choosing a guard
docs.text:
A guard is a named way to log in, like api or web. It says how the login is kept and which model holds the users. Pick the guard driver that fits your app:

Your app Use An API for a mobile app, a front end on another domain, or scripts Access tokens. You can revoke each token, give it abilities and renew it. An API where other services check the token with a key JWT. The token is signed, so there is no token table. Web pages served by this app (forms, Inertia) Session. The browser sends the session cookie. Web pages and an API in one app More than one guard.

If you are not sure, use access tokens for an API.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: These steps start from a new app made with dox create my_app. It has a SQLite database, a User model and a users table with name, email and password columns.

docs.title: Installing
docs.text:
Run dox add auth, then run the migration it writes:

dox add auth

The command adds the dox_auth package, writes the auth config, writes the provider that loads the config, and writes the token table migration. Run dox migrate after it. It needs the ORM and a User model, which a new app has. It never overwrites a file, so it is safe to run twice.

If you do not use the command, add the package with dart pub add dox_auth and write the config and provider below yourself. The command does not write the DTOs, so you always add them yourself.

docs.title: The user model
docs.text:
The password hash must never leave the server. So put it in hidden, and toJson() leaves it out. The model of a new app already does this:

lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users', softDelete: true)
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get fillable => <String>['name', 'email', 'password'];

  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The config lists the guards. Each guard has a driver (how the login is kept) and an AuthProvider (which model holds the users). This config has one guard, api, with access tokens:

lib/config/auth.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

AuthConfig authConfig = AuthConfig(
  defaultGuard: 'api',
  guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
    'api': AuthGuard(
      driver: AccessTokenAuthDriver(expiresIn: const Duration(days: 30)),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
    ),
  },
);

Auth() and AuthMiddleware() use the defaultGuard. All options are in the reference.

docs.title: Loading the config
docs.text:
A DoxProvider gives the config to dox_auth when the app starts. Dox finds every DoxProvider by itself, so you do not register it. Do not mix it up with the AuthProvider of the config:

lib/providers/auth_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/auth.dart';

class AppAuthProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(authConfig);
  }
}

docs.title: Validating the input
docs.text:
You should check the register and login body with DTOs. Bad input then gets a 422, and the controller does not run:

lib/app/dtos/auth/auth.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

part 'auth.dto.g.dart';

/// The body of a register request.
@Dto()
class RegisterUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 1, max: 255)
  final String name;

  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  /// bcrypt reads at most 72 bytes
  @Length(min: 8, max: 72)
  final String password;

  const RegisterUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    required this.password,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<RegisterUser> schema = $RegisterUserDto;
}

/// The body of a login request.
@Dto()
class LoginUser {
  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  final String email;

  final String password;

  const LoginUser({required this.email, required this.password});

  static const DtoSchema<LoginUser> schema = $LoginUserDto;
}

Then run the code generator. It writes the DTO code and adds AppAuthProvider to lib/generated/container.g.dart:

dart run build_runner build

docs.title: Access tokens
docs.text:
An access token is an API token that you can revoke at any time. A token looks like oat_12.<secret>, where 12 is the row id in the token table. The table keeps only a SHA-256 hash of the secret, so you see the plain token only once, when you make it.

The setup above already added the api guard with AccessTokenAuthDriver.

docs.title: Creating the token table
docs.text:
The tokens live in the auth_access_tokens table. dox add auth already wrote its migration. If you set up by hand, write it with this command:

dox auth:tokens-table --users-table=users
dox migrate

--users-table=users adds a foreign key with cascade delete, so when you delete a user, the user's tokens are deleted too. For users with uuid or text ids, see Users with uuid or text ids.

docs.title: Issuing tokens
docs.text:
The controller makes a token on register and on login. Hash.makeAsync and attempt run bcrypt in another isolate, so they do not block the server:

lib/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/dtos/auth/auth.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class AuthController {
  /// POST /api/auth/register: make an account and give a token.
  Future<DoxResponse> register(RegisterUser body) async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email
      ..password = await Hash.makeAsync(body.password);
    await user.save();

    AccessToken token = await Auth().createAccessToken(user, name: 'login');
    return response(<String, dynamic>{
      'token': token.value,
      'user': user,
    }).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/login: check the email and password, give a token.
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> login(DoxRequest req, LoginUser body) async {
    Auth auth = Auth(ip: req.ip());
    String? token = await auth.attempt(<String, dynamic>{
      'email': body.email,
      'password': body.password,
    });
    if (token == null) {
      throw UnAuthorizedException(message: 'Wrong email or password');
    }
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token, 'user': auth.user<User>()};
  }

  /// GET /api/auth/me: the logged-in user.
  User? me(DoxRequest req) {
    return req.auth?.user<User>();
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/logout: the token of this request stops working.
  Future<Map<String, bool>> logout(DoxRequest req) async {
    await (req.auth as Auth).revokeToken(req);
    return <String, bool>{'logged_out': true};
  }
}

attempt finds the user by email and checks the password. It gives a new token with all abilities, or null when the login is wrong. Auth(ip: req.ip()) gives the client ip to the login throttle.

docs.title: Protecting the API routes
docs.text:
Add AuthMiddleware() to a route to protect it. A request with no good token stops with a 401. You should also put a rate limit on register and login, because it slows down password guessing:

lib/routes/api.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/api.controller.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (ApiController c) => c.pong);

    // for guests
    Route.post('/auth/register', <dynamic>[
      RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'register'),
      (AuthController c) => c.register,
    ]);
    Route.post('/auth/login', <dynamic>[
      RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'login'),
      (AuthController c) => c.login,
    ]);

    // for logged-in users
    Route.get('/auth/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (AuthController c) => c.me]);
    Route.post('/auth/logout', <dynamic>[
      AuthMiddleware(),
      (AuthController c) => c.logout,
    ]);
  }
}

Run dart run build_runner build again, then start the app with dox s.

docs.title: Sending the token
docs.text:
The client sends the token in the Authorization header. You can try the flow with curl:

# log in, and keep the token in TOKEN
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ada@example.com","password":"secret-pass"}'
# 200 {"token":"oat_2.OTAG...","user":{"id":1,...}}
TOKEN='oat_2.OTAG...'

curl localhost:3000/api/auth/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 200 {"id":1,"name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com",...}

curl localhost:3000/api/auth/me
# 401 {"code":"unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}

docs.title: Token abilities
docs.text:
An ability is a name like posts:read on a token. It says what the token may do. Sometimes you want a token that can do only a few things, for example a token for a script that only reads posts. Give the abilities when you make the token. The default is *, which means all abilities:

AccessToken token = await auth.createAccessToken(
  auth.user<User>()!,
  name: 'script',
  abilities: <String>['posts:read'],
  expiresIn: const Duration(days: 90),
);

Check an ability in the controller with tokenCan. It is true when the token has the ability or *:

if (!(req.auth as Auth).tokenCan('posts:read')) {
  throw ForbiddenHttpException();
}

AuthMiddleware only checks that the token is good. So a route with no tokenCan check takes every token, and you must check the ability on each route that needs one. tokenCan is always false for a session or JWT login.

You should also guard the routes that make or renew tokens with an ability like tokens:manage. A login token has *, so it passes. A script token does not, so a leaked script token can not make new tokens.

docs.title: Listing and revoking tokens
docs.text:
Use these methods to manage the tokens of a user. A revoked token is deleted from the table, so it stops working at once:

await Auth().accessTokens(user);           // all tokens of the user, newest first, expired ones too
await Auth().revokeAccessToken(user, id);  // false when the user has no token with this id
await Auth().revokeAllAccessTokens(user);  // all tokens of the user, eg. after a password change
await Auth().revokeToken(req);             // the token of this request (a logout)

token.toJson() has no hash and no plain token, so you can send a token list to the client.

Expired tokens stay in the table until you delete them. Run pruneExpiredAccessTokens from a scheduled task:

await Auth().pruneExpiredAccessTokens();   // delete expired tokens, eg. from a scheduled job

docs.title: Rotating tokens
docs.text:
Rotate a token to renew it before it expires. rotateAccessToken makes a new token with the same user, name and abilities, and the old token stops working at once:

/// POST /api/auth/refresh: a new token in place of the token of this
/// request. The old token stops working at once.
Future<Map<String, dynamic>> refresh(DoxRequest req) async {
  Auth auth = req.auth as Auth;
  if (!auth.tokenCan('tokens:manage')) {
    throw ForbiddenHttpException();
  }
  AccessToken next = await auth.rotateAccessToken(auth.currentAccessToken!);
  return <String, dynamic>{
    'token': next.value,
    'expires_at': next.expiresAt?.toIso8601String(),
  };
}

A token can be rotated only once. A second rotate, or a rotate of a revoked or expired token, throws an UnAuthorizedException (401).

If one client sends requests in parallel, a request that is still on the way with the old token would fail. In that case give a short grace, so the old token works a few more seconds. Keep it short, because a stolen old token works on every route in that time:

rotateAccessToken(token, grace: const Duration(seconds: 10))

Each rotate gives the token a full new life. So a client that rotates again and again stays logged in forever. If you want a limit, keep the first login time yourself, or ask for the password again after some time.

docs.title: JWT tokens
docs.text:
A JWT is a signed token. The server keeps no list of tokens, so a token works until it expires, unless you turn on revocation. The user is still loaded from the database on each request, by the id in the token. This way needs no token table.

For a longer walkthrough, see the JWT auth guide.

docs.title: Configuring the JWT guard
docs.text:
Change the guard driver to JwtAuthDriver:

lib/config/auth.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

AuthConfig authConfig = AuthConfig(
  defaultGuard: 'api',
  guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
    'api': AuthGuard(
      driver: JwtAuthDriver(
        secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
        expiresIn: const Duration(days: 7),
        // the token holds only the user id
        minimalPayload: true,
        // lets logout stop a token before it expires
        revocation: true,
      ),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
    ),
  },
);

secret signs the tokens. APP_KEY is fine, because it must be at least 32 bytes. dox key:generate makes a new one. expiresIn is one hour by default.

docs.title: Issuing JWT tokens
docs.text:
The controller and routes are the same as for access tokens, with two changes. On register, Auth().login(user) gives a token with no password check:

String? token = Auth().login(user);

On logout, revoke the token. This needs revocation: true:

await Auth().revokeToken(req);

Login with attempt works the same: it checks the password and gives a JWT.

docs.title: Small tokens
docs.text: Anyone can read a JWT payload, because it is signed, not secret. By default the token holds the user (toJson() without hidden fields). You should set minimalPayload: true, so the token holds only the user id (the sub claim). Then load the user with req.auth?.user<User>(), not from the token.

docs.title: Revoking tokens
docs.text:
By default a JWT works until it expires. Turn on revocation if you want logout to stop a token at once. The driver then keeps revoked tokens in a cache store:

JwtAuthDriver(
  secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
  revocation: true,
  revocationStore: 'auth',
)

Use revokeToken for a logout:

await Auth().revokeToken(req);     // revoke the bearer token of this request (a logout)

Use revokeAllTokens to log a user out everywhere, for example after a password change or a ban:

await Auth().revokeAllTokens(id);  // revoke all tokens of a user, eg. after a password change or a ban

Give auth its own cache store, like redis with its own prefix, and never flush it. A flush brings revoked tokens back until they expire. With revocation off, these methods throw a StateError, so no one thinks a token is revoked when it is not.

docs.title: Changing the secret
docs.text:
Sometimes you must change the signing secret. New tokens are always signed with secret, and old tokens are checked with the old secrets too.

If the secret is APP_KEY, follow Change the key. The old keys in AppConfig.previousKeys are used, so you need nothing more.

If you use a separate JWT secret, give the old one to the driver:

JwtAuthDriver(
  secret: SecretKey(env.jwtSecret),
  previousSecrets: <JWTKey>[SecretKey(env.jwtOldSecret)],
)

Remove the old secret once expiresIn has passed. To log out everyone at once, change the secret and keep no old secrets. Never keep a leaked secret, because anyone who has it can make tokens.

docs.title: Session login for web pages
docs.text: For web pages, keep the login in the session instead of a token. The browser sends the session cookie, so the client does nothing. This needs SessionMiddleware and CsrfMiddleware. See Session and CSRF protection.

docs.title: Configuring the session guard
docs.text:
Use SessionAuthDriver:

lib/config/auth.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

AuthConfig authConfig = AuthConfig(
  defaultGuard: 'web',
  guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
    'web': AuthGuard(
      driver: SessionAuthDriver(),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
    ),
  },
);

docs.title: Logging in
docs.text:
attemptSession checks the password and keeps the user id in the session. loginSession logs a user in with no password check. logout removes the login and all session data. Login and logout also give the session a new id and a new CSRF token.

This controller answers JSON, for a front end with axios or Inertia. axios sends the CSRF token by itself:

lib/app/http/controllers/session.controller.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/dtos/auth/auth.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class SessionController {
  /// POST /register: make an account and log in.
  Future<DoxResponse> register(DoxRequest req, RegisterUser body) async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email
      ..password = await Hash.makeAsync(body.password);
    await user.save();

    Auth().loginSession(req, user);
    return response(user).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// POST /login: check the email and password, keep the login in the session.
  Future<User?> login(DoxRequest req, LoginUser body) async {
    Auth auth = Auth();
    bool ok = await auth.attemptSession(req, <String, dynamic>{
      'email': body.email,
      'password': body.password,
    });
    if (!ok) {
      throw UnAuthorizedException(message: 'Wrong email or password');
    }
    return auth.user<User>();
  }

  /// GET /me: the logged-in user.
  User? me(DoxRequest req) {
    return req.auth?.user<User>();
  }

  /// POST /logout: remove the login and all session data.
  Map<String, bool> logout(DoxRequest req) {
    Auth().logout(req);
    return <String, bool>{'logged_out': true};
  }
}

For an HTML form, answer with a redirect instead. The method then returns Future<DoxResponse>. See CSRF protection for the form token:

if (!ok) {
  req.session.flashErrors(<String, dynamic>{'email': 'Wrong email or password'});
  return back(req);
}
return redirect('/dashboard');

docs.title: Adding the routes
docs.text:
Put the session and CSRF middleware on the web router only, so the API routes stay without a session:

lib/routes/web.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/session.controller.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/web.controller.dart';

class WebRouter extends Router {
  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[
    const SessionMiddleware(),
    const CsrfMiddleware(),
  ];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (WebController c) => c.pong);

    Route.post('/register', <dynamic>[
      RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'register'),
      (SessionController c) => c.register,
    ]);
    Route.post('/login', <dynamic>[
      RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'login'),
      (SessionController c) => c.login,
    ]);
    Route.get('/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (SessionController c) => c.me]);
    Route.post('/logout', <dynamic>[
      AuthMiddleware(),
      (SessionController c) => c.logout,
    ]);
  }
}

docs.title: Redirecting guests
docs.text:
On web pages you often want to send a guest to the login page instead of a 401. Use redirectTo for this:

AuthMiddleware(redirectTo: '/login')

With the jsonNoRedirect flag on, a JSON or XHR client gets a 401 and no redirect.

docs.title: Ending sessions when the password changes
docs.text:
By default, a session stays logged in after the user changes the password, so a stolen session still works. Turn on the endSessionsOnPasswordChange flag to fix this. A password change then ends all sessions of the user on their next request through AuthMiddleware:

lib/config/auth.dart
AuthConfig authConfig = AuthConfig(
  defaultGuard: 'web',
  guards: guards,
  flags: const AuthFlags(endSessionsOnPasswordChange: true),
);

This also ends the current session. If your app changes the password itself, keep the current session with updateSessionPasswordHash after save():

user.password = await Hash.makeAsync(newPassword);
await user.save();
Auth().updateSessionPasswordHash(req, user);

Pass a fully loaded user. A user from a select() with no password column looks like a user with no password, so the session ends.

docs.title: Logging out other devices
docs.text:
logoutOtherDevices ends all other sessions of the user and keeps this one. It checks the password, so it needs the password from a form. It needs a session guard and the flag above:

/// POST /logout-others: end the sessions on other devices.
Future<Map<String, bool>> logoutOthers(DoxRequest req, ConfirmPassword body) async {
  await (req.auth as Auth).logoutOtherDevices(req, body.password);
  return <String, bool>{'done': true};
}

ConfirmPassword is a DTO with one password field, like LoginUser. A wrong password throws an UnAuthorizedException (401, code wrong_password). Because it checks a password, put a rate limit on the route, like on a login.

docs.title: More than one guard
docs.text:
Sometimes one app needs more than one kind of login. For example, a session for web pages, access tokens for the API, and admins in their own table. Each guard has its own driver and its own user model:

lib/config/auth.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/admin/admin.model.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

AuthConfig authConfig = AuthConfig(
  defaultGuard: 'web',
  guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
    'web': AuthGuard(
      driver: SessionAuthDriver(),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
    ),
    'api': AuthGuard(
      driver: AccessTokenAuthDriver(),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
    ),
    'admin': AuthGuard(
      driver: AccessTokenAuthDriver(table: 'admin_access_tokens'),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => Admin()),
    ),
  },
);

Pick a guard by name with guard::

String? token = await Auth(guard: 'admin').attempt(credentials);

Route.get('/admin', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(guard: 'admin'), (AdminController c) => c.index]);

To accept more than one guard on a route, use guards:. The first guard with a good login sets req.auth:

// try the guards in order
Route.get('/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(guards: <String>['web', 'api']), (UserController c) => c.me]);

A token of one guard does not work on another guard. Give each user model its own token table, with table: on the driver and in the migration (AccessTokenTables.up(schema, table: 'admin_access_tokens')).

docs.title: Optional login
docs.text:
A public page may still want to know the user. AuthMiddleware(optional: true) sets req.auth when the login is good, and lets guests through with req.auth as null:

Route.get('/posts', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(optional: true), (PostController c) => c.index]);

docs.title: Pages for guests only
docs.text:
Login and register pages are for guests only. GuestMiddleware sends a logged-in user to redirectTo. With no redirectTo, the answer is a 403:

Route.get('/login', <dynamic>[GuestMiddleware(redirectTo: '/dashboard'), (PageController c) => c.login]);

docs.title: Getting the logged in user
docs.text:
After AuthMiddleware, req.auth holds the login. It is null for a guest:

User? user = req.auth?.user<User>();

req.auth?.id() gives the primary key of the user. For tokenCan and currentAccessToken, cast it: req.auth as Auth.

docs.title: Login throttle
docs.text:
You should limit failed logins, because it stops password guessing on one account. The login throttle is off by default. Turn it on in your auth provider:

lib/providers/auth_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/auth.dart';

class AppAuthProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(authConfig);
    // 5 failed logins a minute. Change it with maxAttempts: and decay:
    Auth.throttle = LoginThrottle();
  }
}

After maxAttempts failed logins for the same email and ip, the next try throws LoginThrottledException (429) until decay has passed. A good login clears the count.

Always pass the ip with Auth(ip: req.ip()). Without an ip, the count is per account only, so anyone can lock an account. attemptSession takes the ip from the request.

The counts live in the app cache. If you run many isolates or servers, use a shared store with LoginThrottle(store: 'redis'). The throttle does not stop many tries sent at the same time, so also keep a RateLimit on the login route.

docs.title: Password hashing
docs.text:
Passwords use bcrypt with cost 10 by default. Each step up doubles the time of a login. If you raise it, set the cost for new hashes and tell the driver, so a login for an unknown email takes as long as a wrong password:

Hash.rounds = 12;
JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(env.appKey), hashRounds: 12);
SessionAuthDriver(hashRounds: 12);
AccessTokenAuthDriver(hashRounds: 12);

Old hashes keep their own cost, so they still work. Hash them again on the next good login:

if (Auth.needsRehash(user.password!)) {
  user.password = await Hash.makeAsync(password);
  await user.save();
  // with a session login and the endSessionsOnPasswordChange flag:
  // Auth().updateSessionPasswordHash(req, user);
}

bcrypt reads at most 72 bytes. A longer password throws an ArgumentError, so limit the length in the DTO. See Hashing.

docs.title: Logging in with another field
docs.text:
attempt searches the user by identifierFields and checks the column in passwordField. Change them if your users log in with a username, or the hash is in another column:

AuthProvider(
  model: () => User(),
  identifierFields: <String>['username'],
  passwordField: 'password_hash',
)

docs.title: Users with uuid or text ids
docs.text:
Access tokens keep the user id in the tokenable_id column, which is a big int by default. If your users have other ids, use the same choice in the migration and on the driver:

  • uuid ids: dox auth:tokens-table --uuid and AccessTokenAuthDriver(uuidIds: true).
  • text ids: dox auth:tokens-table --string-ids and AccessTokenAuthDriver(stringIds: true).

Session and JWT guards need nothing for this.

docs.title: Two-step login (2FA)
docs.text:
A two-step login asks for a password, then for a code from a mail or an app. Your app makes and checks the code. dox_auth helps with tokens:

  1. Step one checks the password with once(), and gives a short token with only the 2fa:pending ability.
  2. Step two checks the code, rotates the token, and gives the new token all abilities with setAccessTokenAbilities.
  3. Each route that needs the second step uses a middleware that refuses 2fa:pending tokens.

The controller with both steps:

lib/app/http/controllers/two_factor.controller.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/dtos/auth/auth.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/dtos/two_factor_code/two_factor_code.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class TwoFactorController {
  /// POST /api/auth/login, step one: check the password. The token
  /// works 10 minutes, and only for step two.
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> login(DoxRequest req, LoginUser body) async {
    Auth auth = Auth(ip: req.ip());
    bool ok = await auth.once(<String, dynamic>{
      'email': body.email,
      'password': body.password,
    });
    if (!ok) {
      throw UnAuthorizedException(message: 'Wrong email or password');
    }
    AccessToken token = await auth.createAccessToken(
      auth.user<User>()!,
      name: 'login',
      abilities: <String>['2fa:pending'],
      expiresIn: const Duration(minutes: 10),
    );
    // send the code to the user here, for example by mail
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token.value, 'two_factor': true};
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/two-factor, step two: check the code. Give a new
  /// token for a full login. The step-one token ends.
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> verify(DoxRequest req, TwoFactorCode body) async {
    Auth auth = req.auth as Auth;
    AccessToken token = auth.currentAccessToken!;
    if (!token.abilities.contains('2fa:pending')) {
      throw ForbiddenHttpException();
    }
    if (!_codeIsGood(auth.user<User>()!, body.code)) {
      throw UnAuthorizedException(message: 'Wrong code');
    }
    // a new token with the expiresIn of the driver. It still has 2fa:pending.
    AccessToken full = await auth.rotateAccessToken(token);
    // all abilities, like a normal login
    await auth.setAccessTokenAbilities(full, <String>['*']);
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': full.value};
  }

  /// Check the code with your own two-step code. Make each code expire,
  /// and limit the wrong tries per user.
  bool _codeIsGood(User user, String code) {
    throw UnimplementedError('check the two-step code');
  }
}

verify checks abilities.contains('2fa:pending'), not tokenCan, because tokenCan is also true for *. Rotate first, then set the abilities, so no token ever has * when a step fails.

The middleware for the routes of a logged-in user. Put it after AuthMiddleware():

lib/app/http/middleware/two_factor.middleware.dart
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// Lets a request through only when its token did the second step.
/// Put it after AuthMiddleware.
dynamic requireTwoFactor(DoxRequest req) {
  Auth? auth = req.auth as Auth?;
  if (auth == null || auth.currentAccessToken == null) {
    throw UnAuthorizedException();
  }
  if (auth.currentAccessToken!.abilities.contains('2fa:pending')) {
    throw ForbiddenHttpException();
  }
  return req;
}

Use TwoFactorController.login as the login route, and add the step-two route with a rate limit:

Route.post('/auth/login', <dynamic>[
  RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'login'),
  (TwoFactorController c) => c.login,
]);
Route.post('/auth/two-factor', <dynamic>[
  RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'two-factor'),
  AuthMiddleware(),
  (TwoFactorController c) => c.verify,
]);

A route without requireTwoFactor still takes a step-one token. Register must give no token, and any other place that gives a token must also do both steps.

docs.title: Checking a login with no request
docs.text:
Code that has no request, like a Socket.IO login, can check a token or a session itself. Both give null when the login is not good:

User? user = await Auth(guard: 'api').userFromToken(token);
User? user = await Auth(guard: 'web').userFromSession(session);

userFromToken runs the same checks as a request, for JWT and access token guards. Give the token without the Bearer prefix. For userFromSession, load the session with SessionMiddleware().fromCookie(value). See Session.

docs.title: Writing your own guard
docs.text:
Sometimes you want to log users in your own way, like with an API key in a header. Write a driver: extend AuthDriver and return the user from verifyToken. AuthMiddleware and req.auth then work as with the other drivers.

This driver finds the user by a SHA-256 hash of the key, so a leak of the table does not leak the keys. It uses the crypto package:

lib/app/auth/api_key_auth_driver.dart
import 'dart:convert';

import 'package:crypto/crypto.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

/// `Authorization: Bearer <api key>` gives the user with this key.
class ApiKeyAuthDriver extends AuthDriver {
  @override
  Future<Model<dynamic>?> verifyToken(IDoxRequest req, String guard) async {
    String header = req.header('Authorization') ?? '';
    if (!header.startsWith('Bearer ')) return null;
    String key = header.substring(7).trim();
    String hash = sha256.convert(utf8.encode(key)).toString();
    Model<dynamic> model = AuthEngine().guard(guard).provider.model();
    return await model.where('api_key_hash', hash).getFirst();
  }

  /// no password login for this guard
  @override
  Future<Model<dynamic>?> attempt(Map<String, dynamic> credentials, String guard) async => null;

  /// no token to make: the key is the token
  @override
  String? createToken(Map<String, dynamic>? userPayload, String guard) => null;
}

Add it as a guard, and use the guard on the route:

'key': AuthGuard(
  driver: ApiKeyAuthDriver(),
  provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
),

Route.get('/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(guard: 'key'), (DoxRequest req) => req.auth?.user<User>()]);

Make each key long and random, like openssl rand -hex 32. Then a fast hash like SHA-256 is safe. Do not use bcrypt here, because you can not search by a bcrypt hash.

If you already have your own middleware, set the user with Auth().setUser(req, user). Then req.auth gives this user:

Auth(guard: 'api').setUser(req, user);

docs.title: When the database fails
docs.text:
The access token check reads the database. When the database fails, the request gets a 401 by default, and the error is reported. But many clients take a 401 as "you are logged out", so a short database problem logs users out. Turn on throwOnError to throw the error instead:

AccessTokenAuthDriver(
  expiresIn: const Duration(days: 30),
  throwOnError: true,
)

The error then goes to your exception handler, which answers 500 by default. To answer 503, so the client tries again, catch the database errors in render:

lib/app/exception_handler.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart' show SqliteException;

class AppExceptionHandler extends ExceptionHandler {
  const AppExceptionHandler();

  @override
  dynamic render(Object error, HttpRequest req) {
    // a database error: ask the client to try again
    if (error is SqliteException ||
        error is PgException ||
        error is MysqlException) {
      return HttpStatusException(503, headers: <String, String>{'retry-after': '5'});
    }
    return super.render(error, req);
  }
}

SqliteException comes from the sqlite3 package (dart pub add sqlite3). On Postgres or MySQL only, drop it. Set the handler with exceptionHandler: const AppExceptionHandler() in AppConfig.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
DoxTestClient runs your app in the test, and withToken sends Authorization: Bearer <token>. This test works for access tokens and JWT. It uses the database of .env, so it runs the migrations first:

test/auth_test.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/testing.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/database.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() {
  late DoxTestClient client;

  setUpAll(() async {
    Dox().initialize(appConfig);
    await Migrator(
      migrations: migrations,
      config: databaseConfig.getConnectionConfig(),
    ).migrate();
    client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig);
  });

  tearDownAll(() async {
    await client.close();
  });

  test('register, then use the token', () async {
    String email = 'test-${DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch}@example.com';
    TestResponse register = await client.post(
      '/api/auth/register',
      body: <String, dynamic>{
        'name': 'Test',
        'email': email,
        'password': 'secret-pass',
      },
    );
    register.expectStatus(201);
    String token = register.json['token'] as String;

    TestResponse me = await client.withToken(token).get('/api/auth/me');
    me.expectStatus(200);
    expect(me.json['email'], email);
    expect(me.json.containsKey('password'), isFalse);
  });

  test('no token gives 401', () async {
    (await client.get('/api/auth/me')).expectStatus(401);
  });
}

To act as a user with no HTTP login, make a token in the test with await Auth().createAccessToken(user), then use client.withToken(token.value!). For a session app, use client.withSession(), which keeps cookies and sends the CSRF token. See Testing.

docs.title: Problems
docs.text: Error Cause Fix LateInitializationError: Field 'config' has not been initialized. Auth.initialize did not run. AppAuthProvider is missing, or the generator did not run. Add AppAuthProvider, then run dart run build_runner build. 401 Authentication failed No Authorization header, a bad, expired or revoked token, a deleted user, or a token of another guard. Send Authorization: Bearer <token>. Log in again. 403 Forbidden The token does not have the ability. Use a token with the ability. See Token abilities. Invalid argument (guard): no auth guard with this name: "admin" A guard name that is not in guards. Fix the name, or add the guard. Bad state: The auth guard 'api' does not use SessionAuthDriver. ... logout, attemptSession or loginSession on a token guard. Use revokeToken(req) to log out a token. Bad state: The auth guard 'api' does not use AccessTokenAuthDriver. An access token method on a JWT or session guard. Use a guard with AccessTokenAuthDriver. Bad state: The auth guard 'web' does not use JwtAuthDriver. revokeAllTokens, forgetUser, userFromToken or revokeToken on a session guard. A session logs out with logout(req). Bad state: AccessTokenAuthDriver makes tokens with Auth().createAccessToken(user), not login(). Auth().login(user) on an access token guard. Use createAccessToken(user). Bad state: revokeToken needs token revocation. ... A revoke method on a JWT guard without revocation. Set revocation: true. See Revoking tokens. Bad state: The table 'auth_access_tokens' has no rotated_at column. ... rotateAccessToken on an old token table. Add the column. See A token table without rotated_at. 401 The access token was already rotated. A second rotate of the same token. Rotate the new token, not the old one. 401 The access token is expired. or is revoked or does not exist. Rotate of an expired or revoked token. Log in again. Invalid argument(s) (secret): The JWT secret is empty. ... JwtAuthDriver with an empty secret. Set APP_KEY with dox key:generate. Invalid argument(s) (secret): The JWT secret is <n> bytes. ... A secret shorter than 32 bytes. In development, local, test and testing it is only a warning. Run dox key:generate. Invalid argument(s) (password): The password is too long. ... A password longer than 72 bytes. Limit the length in the DTO. Invalid argument(s): Set guard or a non-empty guards list, not both. AuthMiddleware with both guard and guards, or guards: []. Set one of them. 429 Too many login attempts. ... The login throttle. Wait retryAfter. 419 CSRF token mismatch A session POST without the CSRF token. See CSRF protection. 403 Already logged in GuestMiddleware with no redirectTo, for a logged-in user. Set redirectTo, or log out first. 401 wrong_password logoutOtherDevices with a wrong password. Show an error on the form. Bad state: logoutOtherDevices() needs the endSessionsOnPasswordChange flag logoutOtherDevices with the flag off. Turn the flag on.

docs.title: 401, 403, 419 and 429
docs.text:
• 401: the user is not logged in. The client should log in again.
  • 403: the user is logged in, but may not do this, like a missing ability or a failed policy.
  • 419: a session request with no CSRF token.
  • 429: too many failed logins.

docs.title: Access tokens
docs.text:
• attempt always gives a token with *.
  • revokeToken(req) on the Auth of AuthMiddleware uses the token that was already checked.
  • last_used_at is written at most once a minute per token. A failed write is reported and the request goes on.
  • tokenable_type is the table name of the user model. If you rename the users table, old tokens stop working.
  • Each token has a type, which is the guard name. If you rename a guard, set AccessTokenAuthDriver(type: 'old-name') to keep its tokens.
  • When you delete a user without --users-table, call revokeAllAccessTokens(user), so old tokens can not match a new user with the same id.
  • The migration makes the table on the default connection. For AccessTokenAuthDriver(connection: 'other'), make it on that connection.
  • rotateAccessToken runs in one transaction. When two rotates of one token run at the same time, only one works. expiresIn: and name: change the new token.
  • A uuid is kept and compared in lower case. Text ids are compared exactly.
  • A token name over 255 characters throws an ArgumentError.
  • On MySQL, expires_at is rounded to the second.

docs.title: A token table without rotated_at
docs.text:
A token table without the rotated_at column works for everything except rotate. To add it, stop dox s, run dox make:migration add_rotated_at_to_auth_access_tokens, and put this in the new file. Then run dox migrate:

// ignore_for_file: file_names
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

class AddRotatedAtToAuthAccessTokens extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.table('auth_access_tokens', (Table t) {
      t.dateTimeTz('rotated_at').nullable();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.table('auth_access_tokens', (Table t) {
      t.dropColumn('rotated_at');
    });
  }
}

docs.title: JWT
docs.text:
• A token is checked with secret first, then with each old secret. An expired token fails at once.
  • The token keeps the guard name in its aud claim, so a token of one guard does not work on another.
  • userCacheTtl keeps the user in memory for this time and skips the query. A deleted or changed user is seen only after it ends, unless forgetUser(id) runs. Each isolate has its own cache.
  • With revocation on, each token check reads the revocation store. Use memory for one isolate, or redis for many. When the store can not be read, the token is checked without it, and a warning is printed once.
  • A revoked token stays on the deny list only until it expires. revokeAllTokens keeps tokens made after the call. It uses the server clock, so keep clocks in sync.
  • The HMAC key is made from secret with HKDF-SHA256 and the label dox:jwt. Another service that checks the tokens needs driver.signingKey.
  • JwtAuthDriver.bearerToken(req) gives the token of a request.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
• The session keeps only the user id. AuthMiddleware loads the user on each request, so a deleted user is logged out.
  • With the default cookie session driver, an old copy of the cookie works until the session lifetime ends. If logout must end old cookies, use the cache session driver.
  • With endSessionsOnPasswordChange, a session made while the flag was off gets its fingerprint on its first checked request. To end all old sessions at once, change APP_KEY without previousKeys, or clear the cache session store.
  • The password column must give the same value on every read, or every session ends.
  • A rehash on login also changes the hash, so call updateSessionPasswordHash after it.

docs.title: Other cases
docs.text:
• attempt runs bcrypt also when no user is found, so the answer time does not tell if an email has an account.
  • once checks the password like attempt, but makes no token and does not touch the session.
  • With optional: true, a database error in the JWT or access token check goes on as a guest and is reported. With the session driver, it gives a 500.
  • Auth.throttle is static, so set it in a provider. If you set it in main(), only the first isolate throttles.
  • Auth.needsRehash(hash, rounds: 12) checks against another cost. Auth.hashCost(hash) gives the cost of a hash.

docs.title: AuthConfig and AuthGuard
docs.text: Option Default What it does AuthConfig(defaultGuard:) required the guard that Auth() and the middleware use when no guard is given AuthConfig(guards:) {} the guards, by name AuthConfig(flags:) AuthFlags() (all off) opt-in behaviors. See Auth flags AuthGuard(driver:) required AccessTokenAuthDriver, JwtAuthDriver, SessionAuthDriver, or your own AuthDriver AuthGuard(provider:) required the AuthProvider: which model holds the users

docs.title: AuthProvider
docs.text: Option Default What it does model required a function that makes a new model, like () => User() identifierFields ['email'] the fields attempt searches by passwordField 'password' the column with the bcrypt hash

docs.text: Method What it does Auth.initialize(AuthConfig) sets the config. Call it once, in a DoxProvider Auth(guard: 'admin') uses another guard from guards. Without guard, it uses defaultGuard Auth(ip: req.ip()) gives the client ip to attempt, for the login throttle Auth.throttle the login throttle. null (off) by default await attempt(credentials) finds the user and checks the password. Gives a token (a JWT, or an access token with all abilities), or null await once(credentials) checks the password like attempt. Gives true or false. It makes no token and does not touch the session login(user) gives a JWT for this user, with no password check setUser(req, user) sets this user on req.auth, with no token and no password check user<T>() the user after attempt, once or login isLoggedIn(), check() true when there is a user guest() true when there is no user id() the primary key of the user, or null. It works when the key is in hidden await userFromToken(token) the user of a JWT or access token, with no request await userFromSession(session) the user of a session, with no request await attemptSession(req, credentials) checks the password and keeps the user id in the session. See Rotating tokens await setAccessTokenAbilities(token, abilities) replaces the whole abilities list of a token await accessTokens(user) all access tokens of the user, newest first await revokeAccessToken(user, id) deletes one access token of the user. false when the user has no such token await revokeAllAccessTokens(user) deletes all access tokens of the user. Gives how many await pruneExpiredAccessTokens() deletes the expired tokens of the table. A query or body field can not set it req.auth as Auth the Auth, for tokenCan, currentAccessToken and revokeToken req.auth?.isLoggedIn() true when a user is loaded req.auth?.id() the primary key of the user, or null req.auth?.user<User>() the user model req.auth?.toJson() the user as a map, without hidden fields

docs.title: AccessTokenAuthDriver
docs.text: Option Default What it does table 'auth_access_tokens' the table of the tokens connection the default connection the dox_orm connection name expiresIn null (no end) how long a new token works hashRounds 10 the bcrypt cost of your stored hashes, for attempt type the guard name the type of the tokens. A token works only on a guard with the same type stringIds false true for users with text ids. Use the same value in the migration uuidIds false true for users with uuid ids. Use the same value in the migration throwOnError false true: an error in a token check is thrown, not turned into a 401. See When the database fails

docs.title: AccessTokenTables.up and dox auth:tokens-table
docs.text:
Option Flag Default What it does table none (edit the migration) 'auth_access_tokens' the table name. Use the same name as the driver table uuidIds --uuid false tokenable_id is a uuid column (UUID on Postgres) stringIds --string-ids false tokenable_id is text. Do not use it with --uuid usersTable --users-table=users none adds a foreign key from tokenable_id to usersKey of this table, with cascade delete. The two id columns must have the same type usersKey --users-key=uid 'id' the key column of usersTable

AccessTokenTables.down(schema, table: 'auth_access_tokens') drops the table. The table has these columns: id, tokenable_type, tokenable_id, type, name, hash, abilities, last_used_at, expires_at, rotated_at, created_at, updated_at. auth:tokens-table is a package command of dox_auth, and it never overwrites a migration that is already there.
